)

Fisher information for a parameter set and what it implies.

Attributes:

Name Type Description parameters tuple[str, ...]

Parameter names, in the order of every matrix axis.

information Tensor

The Fisher matrix F, shape (p, p).

covariance Tensor

The Cramér–Rao bound F^{-1} on the identifiable subspace; inf on the diagonal of a parameter with a component in the null space of F.

std Tensor

Lower bound on the standard deviation of each parameter (inf when the parameter is not identifiable from these observations).

correlation Tensor

Correlation matrix of the bound (nan where undefined).

identifiable Tensor

Per parameter, whether it lies outside the null space of F.

eigenvalues Tensor

Eigenvalues of F, descending.

eigenvectors Tensor

Columns are the corresponding parameter directions.

condition_number float

Ratio of the largest to the smallest eigenvalue (inf when F is singular).

std / |true value| per parameter (inf when not identifiable).

def relative_std(self, true_values: dict[str, float]) -> dict[str, float]:
    """``std / |true value|`` per parameter (``inf`` when not identifiable)."""
    return {
        name: float(self.std[i]) / abs(float(true_values[name]))
        for i, name in enumerate(self.parameters)
    }

docs.text:
surrogate_sensitivities(
    pde,
    model,
    parameters,
    x,
    t,
    *,
    n_collocation=2048,
    damping=0.001,
    cg_iterations=300,
    cg_tol=1e-05,
    seed=0,
)

du/dtheta at (x, t) from the trained surrogate, by the implicit-function theorem.

Pass the same pde the model was trained with: the Hessian is taken of that object's physics loss (its loss weights, boundary and initial point counts, loss function and device), at the current values of its parameters. Parameters that are not registered as trainable are made trainable for the duration of the call, so a forward-trained problem works as it is.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default pde Any

The problem the model was trained on.

required model Module

The trained network, a minimum of the physics loss for the parameters' current values.

required parameters Sequence[str]

Names of the PDE parameters to differentiate with respect to.

required x Tensor

Spatial coordinates of the observation points, (N, d).

required t Tensor | None

Time, (N, 1); None for a steady problem (the network then receives t = 0, as the trainer does).

required n_collocation int

Collocation points on which the Hessian is evaluated.

2048 damping float

Tikhonov damping lambda added to H_ww (the Hessian of a trained network is singular along flat directions). When the damped Hessian still shows negative curvature, which happens when the network is not at an exact minimum, the solve restarts with ten times the damping, up to six times.

0.001 cg_iterations int

Maximum conjugate-gradient iterations per parameter.

300 cg_tol float

Relative residual at which the solve stops.

1e-05 seed int

Seed of the collocation sample (drawn in a forked RNG, so the caller's random state is untouched).

0

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If a name is not a parameter of pde, or a solve diverges.

Source code in pinnrl/analysis/surrogate.py 
def surrogate_sensitivities(
    pde: Any,
    model: torch.nn.Module,
    parameters: Sequence[str],
    x: torch.Tensor,
    t: torch.Tensor | None,
    *,
    n_collocation: int = 2048,
    damping: float = 1e-3,
    cg_iterations: int = 300,
    cg_tol: float = 1e-5,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> SurrogateSensitivity:
    """``du/dtheta`` at ``(x, t)`` from the trained surrogate, by the implicit-function theorem.

    Pass the same ``pde`` the model was trained with: the Hessian is taken of
    that object's physics loss (its loss weights, boundary and initial point
    counts, loss function and device), at the current values of its
    parameters. Parameters that are not registered as trainable are made
    trainable for the duration of the call, so a forward-trained problem works
    as it is.

    Args:
        pde: The problem the model was trained on.
        model: The trained network, a minimum of the physics loss for the
            parameters' current values.
        parameters: Names of the PDE parameters to differentiate with respect to.
        x: Spatial coordinates of the observation points, ``(N, d)``.
        t: Time, ``(N, 1)``; ``None`` for a steady problem (the network then
            receives ``t = 0``, as the trainer does).
        n_collocation: Collocation points on which the Hessian is evaluated.
        damping: Tikhonov damping ``lambda`` added to ``H_ww`` (the Hessian of
            a trained network is singular along flat directions). When the
            damped Hessian still shows negative curvature, which happens when
            the network is not at an exact minimum, the solve restarts with
            ten times the damping, up to six times.
        cg_iterations: Maximum conjugate-gradient iterations per parameter.
        cg_tol: Relative residual at which the solve stops.
        seed: Seed of the collocation sample (drawn in a forked RNG, so the
            caller's random state is untouched).

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a name is not a parameter of ``pde``, or a solve diverges.
    """
    unknown = [p for p in parameters if p not in getattr(pde, "parameters", {})]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(f"{unknown} are not parameters of {pde.config.name}")
    device = next(model.parameters()).device
    was_training = model.training
    model.eval()
    try:
        with _temporarily_trainable(pde, parameters) as thetas:
            result = _sensitivities(
                pde,
                model,
                parameters,
                thetas,
                x,
                t,
                device,
                n_collocation,
                damping,
                cg_iterations,
                cg_tol,
                seed,
            )
    finally:
        if was_training:
            model.train()
    return result

loss_hessian_spectrum(
    loss_fn, parameters, iterations=50, seed=0
)

Extreme eigenvalues of d^2 loss / d parameters^2 by Lanczos with full reorthogonalization.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default loss_fn Callable[[], Tensor]

Returns the scalar loss as a function of parameters (it is called once; the graph is kept for Hessian-vector products).

required parameters list[Parameter]

The tensors to differentiate with respect to.

required iterations int

Lanczos steps, hence the number of Ritz values. With 50 steps the few largest and smallest eigenvalues are converged to several digits for typical PINN Hessians.

50 seed int

0 Source code in pinnrl/analysis/spectrum.py 
def loss_hessian_spectrum(
    loss_fn: Callable[[], torch.Tensor],
    parameters: list[torch.nn.Parameter],
    iterations: int = 50,
    seed: int = 0,
) -> HessianSpectrum:
    """Extreme eigenvalues of ``d^2 loss / d parameters^2`` by Lanczos with full reorthogonalization.

    Args:
        loss_fn: Returns the scalar loss as a function of ``parameters`` (it is
            called once; the graph is kept for Hessian-vector products).
        parameters: The tensors to differentiate with respect to.
        iterations: Lanczos steps, hence the number of Ritz values. With 50
            steps the few largest and smallest eigenvalues are converged to
            several digits for typical PINN Hessians.
        seed: Seed of the starting vector (a forked RNG, so the caller's state
            is untouched).
    """
    loss = loss_fn()
    grads = torch.autograd.grad(loss, parameters, create_graph=True, allow_unused=True)
    flat_g = torch.cat(
        [
            (g if g is not None else torch.zeros_like(p)).reshape(-1)
            for g, p in zip(grads, parameters, strict=True)
        ]
    )

    def hvp(v: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        hv = torch.autograd.grad(flat_g @ v, parameters, retain_graph=True, allow_unused=True)
        return torch.cat(
            [
                (h if h is not None else torch.zeros_like(p)).reshape(-1)
                for h, p in zip(hv, parameters, strict=True)
            ]
        )

    n = flat_g.numel()
    m = min(iterations, n)
    with torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[]):
        torch.manual_seed(seed)
        q = torch.randn(n, device=flat_g.device, dtype=flat_g.dtype)
    q = q / q.norm()
    Q = [q]
    alphas: list[float] = []
    betas: list[float] = []
    for k in range(m):
        z = hvp(Q[k]).detach()
        alpha = float(Q[k] @ z)
        z = z - alpha * Q[k] - (betas[-1] * Q[k - 1] if k else 0.0)
        # Full reorthogonalization keeps the Ritz values honest at this size.
        for qq in Q:
            z = z - (qq @ z) * qq
        beta = float(z.norm())
        alphas.append(alpha)
        if beta < 1e-10 or k == m - 1:
            break
        betas.append(beta)
        Q.append(z / beta)
    T = torch.diag(torch.tensor(alphas, dtype=torch.float64))
    if betas:
        off = torch.tensor(betas[: len(alphas) - 1], dtype=torch.float64)
        T += torch.diag(off, 1) + torch.diag(off, -1)
    ritz = torch.linalg.eigvalsh(T).flip(0)
    return HessianSpectrum(eigenvalues=ritz, iterations=len(alphas), loss=float(loss.detach()))

def tangent_kernel_spectrum(
    model: torch.nn.Module,
    values_fn: Callable[[torch.nn.Module], torch.Tensor],
) -> KernelSpectrum:
    """Spectrum of the tangent kernel of a per-point quantity of the network.

    Args:
        model: The network.
        values_fn: Maps the network to the per-point values of the term, shape
            ``(N,)`` or ``(N, k)``: the residual on collocation points, the
            boundary mismatch, the network output itself, ... Derivatives
            inside it must be taken with ``create_graph=True`` so that the
            values stay differentiable with respect to the weights.

    The kernel is ``K = J J^T`` with ``J = d values / d weights`` of shape
    ``(N k, P)``, assembled row by row with one backward pass per value, so
    keep ``N k`` in the hundreds.
    """
    params = [p for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad]
    values = values_fn(model).reshape(-1)
    rows = []
    for i in range(values.numel()):
        grads = torch.autograd.grad(values[i], params, retain_graph=True, allow_unused=True)
        rows.append(
            torch.cat(
                [
                    (g if g is not None else torch.zeros_like(p)).reshape(-1)
                    for g, p in zip(grads, params, strict=True)
                ]
            )
        )
    J = torch.stack(rows).double()
    K = J @ J.T
    eig = torch.linalg.eigvalsh(K).flip(0).clamp_min(0)
    return KernelSpectrum(eigenvalues=eig, trace=float(eig.sum()))

def perturb_observations(
    obs: Observations,
    kind: str,
    magnitude: float,
    *,
    seed: int = 0,
    sensors: torch.Tensor | None = None,
) -> Observations:
    """A disturbed copy of ``{"x", "t", "u"}`` observations.

    Args:
        obs: Observation tensors of shape ``(N, d)``, ``(N, 1)``, ``(N, k)``.
        kind: One of
            ``"noise"`` (add Gaussian noise of standard deviation ``magnitude``),
            ``"bias"`` (add the constant ``magnitude`` to the values),
            ``"dropout"`` (remove a fraction ``magnitude`` of the points at random),
            ``"delay"`` (the values are attributed to times ``t + magnitude``:
            a sensor whose timestamps lag the physics),
            ``"outliers"`` (replace a fraction ``magnitude`` of the values by
            draws of ten times the data's standard deviation).
        magnitude: Size of the disturbance, in the units the kind names.
        seed: Seed of the random draws.
        sensors: Optional boolean mask ``(N,)`` selecting the points a
            ``"bias"`` or ``"delay"`` applies to (a single faulty probe);
            all points by default.

    Raises:
        ValueError: For an unknown kind.
    """
    gen = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(seed)
    x, t, u = obs["x"].clone(), obs["t"].clone(), obs["u"].clone()
    n = u.shape[0]
    mask = torch.ones(n, dtype=torch.bool) if sensors is None else sensors.bool().cpu()
    if kind == "noise":
        u = u + magnitude * torch.randn(u.shape, generator=gen).to(u)
    elif kind == "bias":
        u[mask] = u[mask] + magnitude
    elif kind == "dropout":
        keep = torch.rand(n, generator=gen) >= magnitude
        x, t, u = x[keep], t[keep], u[keep]
    elif kind == "delay":
        t[mask] = t[mask] + magnitude
    elif kind == "outliers":
        hit = torch.rand(n, generator=gen) < magnitude
        scale = 10.0 * float(u.std())
        u[hit] = scale * torch.randn((int(hit.sum()), u.shape[1]), generator=gen).to(u)
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"unknown disturbance {kind!r}; use noise, bias, dropout, delay or outliers"
        )
    return {"x": x, "t": t, "u": u}

linear_response(jacobian, sigma, delta_y)

First-order parameter shift for a data disturbance delta_y.

delta_theta = (J^T Sigma^-1 J)^-1 J^T Sigma^-1 delta_y with Sigma = sigma^2 I, the response of a weighted least-squares estimate. A (N, k, p) Jacobian is flattened over k; delta_y is (N,) or (N, k). Returns (p,).

Source code in pinnrl/analysis/disturbance.py 
def linear_response(
    jacobian: torch.Tensor, sigma: float | torch.Tensor, delta_y: torch.Tensor
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """First-order parameter shift for a data disturbance ``delta_y``.

    ``delta_theta = (J^T Sigma^-1 J)^-1 J^T Sigma^-1 delta_y`` with
    ``Sigma = sigma^2 I``, the response of a weighted least-squares estimate.
    A ``(N, k, p)`` Jacobian is flattened over ``k``; ``delta_y`` is ``(N,)``
    or ``(N, k)``. Returns ``(p,)``.
    """
    J = jacobian.reshape(-1, jacobian.shape[-1]).double()
    d = delta_y.reshape(-1).double()
    if isinstance(sigma, torch.Tensor):
        s = sigma.reshape(-1).double()
        if s.numel() == 1:
            s = s.expand(J.shape[0])
        Jw, dw = J / s[:, None], d / s
    else:
        Jw, dw = J / float(sigma), d / float(sigma)
    F = Jw.T @ Jw
    return torch.linalg.solve(F, Jw.T @ dw)

stability_ratio(pde, model, n_points=8192, seed=0)

error / residual of a trained surrogate on a dense independent sample of the domain.

The residual is the equation applied to the network at fresh uniform points (not the training points), so it includes the quadrature gap; the error is against the closed form. Requires pde.has_exact_solution.

Source code in pinnrl/analysis/disturbance.py 
def stability_ratio(
    pde: Any, model: torch.nn.Module, n_points: int = 8192, seed: int = 0
) -> StabilityRatio:
    """``error / residual`` of a trained surrogate on a dense independent sample of the domain.

    The residual is the equation applied to the network at fresh uniform
    points (not the training points), so it includes the quadrature gap;
    the error is against the closed form. Requires ``pde.has_exact_solution``.
    """
    if not pde.has_exact_solution:
        raise ValueError(f"{pde.config.name}: stability_ratio needs an exact solution")
    was_training = model.training
    model.eval()
    gen = torch.Generator(device="cpu").manual_seed(seed)
    d = max(int(pde.dimension), 1)
    lo = torch.tensor([a for a, _ in pde.domain[:d]], dtype=torch.float32)
    hi = torch.tensor([b for _, b in pde.domain[:d]], dtype=torch.float32)
    t0, t1 = pde.time_domain
    x = (lo + (hi - lo) * torch.rand(n_points, d, generator=gen)).to(pde.device)
    t = (t0 + (t1 - t0) * torch.rand(n_points, 1, generator=gen)).to(pde.device)
    residual = pde.compute_residual(model, x, t).detach()
    with torch.no_grad():
        u = model(torch.cat([x, t], dim=1))
        exact = pde.exact_solution(x, t)
        u = u[:, : exact.shape[1]]
        err = float((u - exact).norm() / exact.norm().clamp_min(1e-12))
        # Boundary: both faces of the first spatial axis at the sampled times.
        xb = torch.cat([x.clone(), x.clone()])
        xb[:n_points, 0], xb[n_points:, 0] = lo[0], hi[0]
        tb = torch.cat([t, t])
        ub = model(torch.cat([xb, tb], dim=1))[:, : exact.shape[1]]
        b_err = float((ub - pde.exact_solution(xb, tb)).pow(2).mean().sqrt())
        i_err = 0.0
        if pde.time_dependent and pde.initial_condition is not None:
            ti = torch.full((n_points, 1), float(t0), device=pde.device)
            ui = model(torch.cat([x, ti], dim=1))[:, : exact.shape[1]]
            i_err = float((ui - pde.initial_condition(x, ti)).pow(2).mean().sqrt())
    res = float(residual.pow(2).mean().sqrt())
    if was_training:
        model.train()
    return StabilityRatio(
        error=err,
        residual=res,
        boundary_error=b_err,
        initial_error=i_err,
        ratio=err / res if res > 0 else float("inf"),
        points=n_points,
    )

field_response(
    model_base, model_perturbed, x, t, reference_delta=None

Change of the trained field between a base and a perturbed problem, on (x, t).

Returns the relative L2 norm of u_perturbed - u_base and, when the reference solution's change reference_delta is given, the amplification ratio ||delta u_PINN|| / ||delta u_ref|| and the relative error of the PINN's response.

Source code in pinnrl/analysis/disturbance.py 
def field_response(
    model_base: torch.nn.Module,
    model_perturbed: torch.nn.Module,
    x: torch.Tensor,
    t: torch.Tensor,
    reference_delta: torch.Tensor | None = None,
) -> dict[str, float]:
    """Change of the trained field between a base and a perturbed problem, on ``(x, t)``.

    Returns the relative L2 norm of ``u_perturbed - u_base`` and, when the
    reference solution's change ``reference_delta`` is given, the
    amplification ratio ``||delta u_PINN|| / ||delta u_ref||`` and the
    relative error of the PINN's response.
    """
    inputs = torch.cat([x, t], dim=1)
    with torch.no_grad():
        ub = model_base(inputs)[:, :1]
        up = model_perturbed(inputs)[:, :1]
    delta = up - ub
    out = {"response": float(delta.norm() / ub.norm().clamp_min(1e-12))}
    if reference_delta is not None:
        ref = reference_delta.reshape(delta.shape)
        out["amplification"] = float(delta.norm() / ref.norm().clamp_min(1e-12))
        out["response_error"] = float((delta - ref).norm() / ref.norm().clamp_min(1e-12))
    return out

def posterior_covariance(
    information_matrix: np.ndarray, prior_std: Sequence[float] | np.ndarray | None = None
) -> np.ndarray:
    """``(P0^-1 + F)^-1`` for the information ``F`` and independent Gaussian priors.

    Args:
        information_matrix: ``F``, ``(p, p)``; the sum of :func:`information`
            over the measurement blocks of a design.
        prior_std: Prior standard deviation of each parameter, ``inf`` for a
            flat prior; ``None`` for all flat.

    Raises:
        numpy.linalg.LinAlgError: When the design and the prior together leave
            a direction of parameter space undetermined.
    """
    F = np.asarray(information_matrix, dtype=float)
    A = F + _prior_precision(prior_std, F.shape[0])
    scale = np.sqrt(np.clip(np.diag(A), 1e-300, None))  # the parameters differ by many decades
    An = A / np.outer(scale, scale)
    if np.linalg.cond(An) > 1e13:
        raise np.linalg.LinAlgError(
            "the design and the prior leave a direction of the parameters undetermined"
        )
    return np.linalg.inv(An) / np.outer(scale, scale)

def information_gain(prior_covariance: np.ndarray, covariance: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """The expected information gain ``0.5 log(det P0 / det P)`` in nats.

    For a linear-Gaussian model this is the mutual information between the
    parameters and the records, the expected Kullback–Leibler divergence from
    prior to posterior. Both covariances must be proper (finite priors).
    """
    _, a = np.linalg.slogdet(np.asarray(prior_covariance, dtype=float))
    _, b = np.linalg.slogdet(np.asarray(covariance, dtype=float))
    return float(0.5 * (a - b))

            anyway, ``(p, p)``.
        target: ``a`` (or a matrix ``A``): minimise the variance of
            ``a^T theta`` (c-optimality). Without it, maximise the
            log-determinant of the posterior precision (D-optimality).
        repeat: Whether a candidate may be picked more than once (replicates).

    Returns:
        :class:`DesignResult`. Greedy selection is not guaranteed optimal; for
        the D criterion it is within ``1 - 1/e`` of the best information gain
        (the gain is submodular), and on the problems of J09 it matches
        exhaustive search.

    Raises:
        ValueError: For ``k`` larger than the number of candidates without ``repeat``.
    """
    blocks = [np.atleast_2d(np.asarray(c, dtype=float)) for c in candidates]
    if not blocks:
        raise ValueError("greedy_design needs at least one candidate")
    p = blocks[0].shape[1]
    noises: Sequence[Any] = (
        [noise] * len(blocks)
        if np.isscalar(noise) or isinstance(noise, np.ndarray)
        else cast("Sequence[Any]", noise)
    )
    if len(noises) != len(blocks):
        raise ValueError("noise needs one entry per candidate")
    infos = [information(b, s) for b, s in zip(blocks, noises, strict=True)]
    if k > len(blocks) and not repeat:
        raise ValueError(f"cannot pick {k} of {len(blocks)} candidates without repeat")
    F = np.zeros((p, p)) if base_information is None else np.array(base_information, dtype=float)
    prior = _prior_precision(prior_std, p)

    def score(Fi: np.ndarray) -> float:
        if target is None:
            sign, logdet = np.linalg.slogdet(Fi + prior)
            return float(-logdet) if sign > 0 else float("inf")
        try:
            return target_std(posterior_covariance(Fi + prior), target)
        except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
            return float("inf")

    result = DesignResult(criterion=[score(F)])
    available = set(range(len(blocks)))
    for _ in range(int(k)):
        scores = {i: score(F + infos[i]) for i in sorted(available)}
        best = min(scores, key=lambda i: (scores[i], i))
        result.chosen.append(best)
        result.criterion.append(scores[best])
        F = F + infos[best]
        if not repeat:
            available.discard(best)
    try:
        result.covariance = posterior_covariance(F + prior)
    except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
        result.covariance = None
    return result

def relative_l2(self, u_pred: np.ndarray) -> float:
    """``||u_pred - u||_2 / ||u||_2`` over the grid."""
    u_ref = self.u.reshape(-1)
    diff = np.asarray(u_pred).reshape(-1) - u_ref
    return float(np.linalg.norm(diff) / np.linalg.norm(u_ref))

def interpolate(self, x: np.ndarray, t: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    """Bilinear interpolation of the field at scattered ``(x, t)`` (any matching shapes)."""
    from scipy.interpolate import RegularGridInterpolator

    interp = RegularGridInterpolator(
        (self.x, self.t), self.u, method="linear", bounds_error=False, fill_value=None
    )
    x = np.asarray(x, dtype=float)
    pts = np.stack([x.reshape(-1), np.asarray(t, dtype=float).reshape(-1)], axis=1)
    return interp(pts).reshape(x.shape)

def as_exact_solution(self) -> Callable:
    """A callable ``u(x, t) -> (N, 1)`` over torch tensors, for ``CustomPDE(exact_solution=...)``."""
    import torch

    def exact(x: torch.Tensor, t: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
        vals = self.interpolate(x[:, 0:1].detach().cpu().numpy(), t.detach().cpu().numpy())
        return torch.as_tensor(vals, dtype=x.dtype, device=x.device).reshape(-1, 1)

    return exact

def burgers_reference(
    nu: float = 0.01 / np.pi,
    nx: int = 256,
    nt: int = 101,
    t_max: float = 1.0,
    n_quad: int = 6001,
    z_max: float = 15.0,
) -> ReferenceSolution:
    """Burgers ``u_t + u u_x = nu u_xx`` on ``[-1, 1]`` with ``u0 = -sin(pi x)``.

    Cole-Hopf gives

        u(x, t) = -∫ sin(pi (x - η)) f(x - η) G(η, t) dη / ∫ f(x - η) G(η, t) dη

    with ``f(y) = exp(-cos(pi y) / (2 pi nu))`` and the heat kernel ``G``.
    Substituting ``η = sqrt(4 nu t) z`` turns ``G`` into ``exp(-z²)``; the
    integrand is periodic times Gaussian, so the trapezoid rule converges
    spectrally. ``z_max = 15`` keeps the far peaks of ``f`` (which dominate
    near ``x = 0`` once the shock forms) inside the window.

    Args:
        nu: Viscosity. The default is the classic ``0.01 / pi`` benchmark.
        nx: Number of spatial grid points on ``[-1, 1]``.
        nt: Number of time grid points on ``[0, t_max]``.
        t_max: Final time.
        n_quad: Trapezoid nodes on ``[-z_max, z_max]``.
        z_max: Half-width of the quadrature window in ``z``.

    Returns:
        The reference field on the ``(nx, nt)`` grid.
    """
    x = np.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, nx)
    t = np.linspace(0.0, t_max, nt)
    u = burgers_cole_hopf(x[:, None], t[None, :], nu, n_quad=n_quad, z_max=z_max)
    return ReferenceSolution(x=x, t=t, u=u)

def allen_cahn_reference(
    epsilon: float = np.sqrt(0.0002),
    t_max: float = 5.0,
    nx: int = 257,
    nt: int = 101,
    refine: int = 8,
    boundary_value: float = -1.0,
) -> ReferenceSolution:
    """Allen-Cahn ``u_t = eps² u_xx + u - u³`` on ``[-1, 1]``, ``u0 = x² cos(pi x)``.

    Dirichlet ``u(±1, t) = boundary_value``. The defaults are the
    ``u_t = 0.001 u_xx + 5 (u - u³)`` benchmark on ``t ∈ [0, 1]`` rewritten
    in the time variable ``τ = 5 t``, which matches the reaction coefficient
    of :class:`pinnrl.pdes.allen_cahn.AllenCahnEquation`.

    The solver grid is ``refine`` times finer than the output grid and the
    output points are a subset of it, so no interpolation error enters.

    Args:
        epsilon: Interface parameter in the residual ``u_t - eps² u_xx - u + u³``.
        t_max: Final time.
        nx: Output spatial points on ``[-1, 1]``.
        nt: Output time points on ``[0, t_max]``.
        refine: Solver-grid refinement factor relative to the output grid.
        boundary_value: Dirichlet value at both ends.

    Returns:
        The reference field on the ``(nx, nt)`` grid.
    """
    n_fine = (nx - 1) * refine + 1
    x_fine = np.linspace(-1.0, 1.0, n_fine)
    dx = x_fine[1] - x_fine[0]
    t = np.linspace(0.0, t_max, nt)
    eps2 = epsilon**2

    u0 = x_fine**2 * np.cos(np.pi * x_fine)

    def rhs(_t: float, v: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        full = np.concatenate(([boundary_value], v, [boundary_value]))
        u_xx = (full[2:] - 2.0 * full[1:-1] + full[:-2]) / dx**2
        return eps2 * u_xx + v - v**3

    sol = solve_ivp(rhs, (0.0, t_max), u0[1:-1], t_eval=t, method="RK45", rtol=1e-9, atol=1e-11)
    if not sol.success:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Allen-Cahn reference solve failed: {sol.message}")

    u_fine = np.empty((n_fine, nt))
    u_fine[0, :] = boundary_value
    u_fine[-1, :] = boundary_value
    u_fine[1:-1, :] = sol.y
    return ReferenceSolution(x=x_fine[::refine], t=t, u=u_fine[::refine, :])

def heat_variable_reference(
    alpha: Callable[[np.ndarray, float], np.ndarray],
    u0: Callable[[np.ndarray], np.ndarray] | None = None,
    domain: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 1.0),
    t_max: float = 1.0,
    nx: int = 201,
    nt: int = 201,
    refine: int = 4,
    boundary_values: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 0.0),
) -> ReferenceSolution:
    """Heat equation with a variable coefficient, ``u_t = (alpha(x, t) u_x)_x``, Dirichlet ends.

    The conservative form is discretised with the coefficient at the cell faces,
    ``(alpha_{i+1/2} (u_{i+1} - u_i) - alpha_{i-1/2} (u_i - u_{i-1})) / dx²``,
    and integrated in time with the implicit BDF method (the system is stiff).
    When ``alpha`` depends on ``t`` only, this is ``u_t = alpha(t) u_xx``; the
    solution for ``u0 = sin(pi x)`` is then ``exp(-pi² ∫alpha) sin(pi x)``, which
    the tests check against.

    Args:
        alpha: ``alpha(x, t) -> array like x`` with ``x`` a NumPy array and ``t`` a float.
        u0: Initial condition ``u0(x)``; default ``sin(pi (x - x_lo) / (x_hi - x_lo))``.
        domain: Spatial interval.
        t_max: Final time.
        nx: Output spatial points (including both ends).
        nt: Output time points on ``[0, t_max]``.
        refine: Solver-grid refinement factor relative to the output grid.
        boundary_values: Dirichlet values at ``x_lo`` and ``x_hi``.

    Returns:
        The reference field on the ``(nx, nt)`` output grid.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: If the time integrator fails.
    """
    x_lo, x_hi = float(domain[0]), float(domain[1])
    n_fine = (nx - 1) * refine + 1
    x_fine = np.linspace(x_lo, x_hi, n_fine)
    dx = x_fine[1] - x_fine[0]
    x_faces = 0.5 * (x_fine[1:] + x_fine[:-1])
    t = np.linspace(0.0, t_max, nt)
    lo_val, hi_val = float(boundary_values[0]), float(boundary_values[1])

    if u0 is None:
        u_init = np.sin(np.pi * (x_fine - x_lo) / (x_hi - x_lo))
    else:
        u_init = np.asarray(u0(x_fine), dtype=float)

    def rhs(tau: float, v: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
        full = np.concatenate(([lo_val], v, [hi_val]))
        a = np.broadcast_to(np.asarray(alpha(x_faces, float(tau)), dtype=float), x_faces.shape)
        flux = a * (full[1:] - full[:-1]) / dx
        return (flux[1:] - flux[:-1]) / dx

    sol = solve_ivp(rhs, (0.0, t_max), u_init[1:-1], t_eval=t, method="BDF", rtol=1e-8, atol=1e-10)
    if not sol.success:
        raise RuntimeError(f"variable-coefficient heat reference failed: {sol.message}")

    u_fine = np.empty((n_fine, nt))
    u_fine[0, :] = lo_val
    u_fine[-1, :] = hi_val
    u_fine[1:-1, :] = sol.y
    return ReferenceSolution(x=x_fine[::refine], t=t, u=u_fine[::refine, :])

def run_sampling_study(
    pdes: Sequence[str] = STUDY_PDES,
    strategies: Sequence[str] = STUDY_STRATEGIES,
    seeds: Sequence[int] = tuple(range(10)),
    settings: StudySettings | None = None,
    workers: int = 1,
    on_result: Callable[[StudyRun], None] | None = None,
) -> list[StudyRun]:
    """Run every ``(pde, strategy, seed)`` combination.

    Tasks are ordered by PDE, then seed, then strategy, so the strategies for
    one seed run side by side under similar machine load. ``workers > 1`` uses a spawn-based
    process pool; ``workers = 1`` runs inline.

    Args:
        pdes: Subset of :data:`STUDY_PDES`.
        strategies: Subset of :data:`STUDY_STRATEGIES`.
        seeds: Seeds to run; each fixes the initial weights.
        settings: Shared study settings.
        workers: Parallel worker processes.
        on_result: Optional callback invoked as each run finishes.

    Returns:
        One :class:`StudyRun` per combination, in task order.
    """
    settings = settings or StudySettings()
    for name in pdes:
        _check_pde(name)
    for name in strategies:
        if name not in STUDY_STRATEGIES:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown strategy {name!r}. Supported: {STUDY_STRATEGIES}")

    references = {name: build_reference(name) for name in pdes}
    tasks = [
        (pde, strategy, seed, settings, references[pde])
        for pde in pdes
        for seed in seeds
        for strategy in strategies
    ]

    results: list[StudyRun] = []
    if workers <= 1:
        for task in tasks:
            run = run_study_case(*task)
            results.append(run)
            if on_result:
                on_result(run)
        return results

    with ProcessPoolExecutor(max_workers=workers, mp_context=mp.get_context("spawn")) as pool:
        for run in pool.map(_worker, tasks):
            results.append(run)
            if on_result:
                on_result(run)
    return results

def run_study_case(
    pde_name: str,
    strategy: str,
    seed: int,
    settings: StudySettings,
    reference: ReferenceSolution,
    device: torch.device | None = None,
) -> StudyRun:
    """Train one PINN for ``settings.num_steps`` steps under one sampler."""
    _check_pde(pde_name)
    if strategy not in STUDY_STRATEGIES:
        raise ValueError(f"Unknown strategy {strategy!r}. Supported: {STUDY_STRATEGIES}")
    chunk = settings.chunk
    if chunk * settings.n_checkpoints != settings.num_steps or chunk % settings.resample_every:
        raise ValueError(
            "num_steps must split into n_checkpoints chunks that are each a multiple "
            f"of resample_every (got {settings.num_steps}, {settings.n_checkpoints}, "
            f"{settings.resample_every})."
        )
    device = device or torch.device("cpu")

    torch.manual_seed(seed)
    np.random.seed(seed)
    pde = _build_pde(pde_name, device)
    trainer = _build_trainer(pde, settings, device)
    torch.manual_seed(seed + 10_000)  # sampling stream, independent of the init

    overhead = {"evals": 0}
    progress = {"value": 0.0}
    sampler = _make_sampler(strategy, pde, settings, device, overhead)
    resample_every = 1 if strategy in _EVERY_STEP else settings.resample_every

    def sample_fn(model, _chunk_progress):
        return sampler(model, progress["value"])

    run = StudyRun(pde_name, strategy, seed, float("nan"), 0, 0.0, 0)
    for _ in range(settings.n_checkpoints):
        out = trainer.train_steps(
            num_steps=chunk, sample_fn=sample_fn, resample_every=resample_every
        )
        run.steps += out["steps"]
        run.train_time_s += out["train_time_s"]
        progress["value"] = run.steps / settings.num_steps
        run.residual_evals = run.steps * settings.n_collocation + overhead["evals"]
        run.curve_step.append(run.steps)
        run.curve_time_s.append(run.train_time_s)
        run.curve_evals.append(run.residual_evals)
        run.curve_rel_l2.append(_relative_l2(trainer.model, reference, device))
    run.rel_l2 = run.curve_rel_l2[-1]
    return run

def summarize(runs: Sequence[StudyRun], budget: str = "steps") -> list[StudySummary]:
    """Median/IQR per ``(pde, strategy)`` plus a paired comparison against ``uniform``.

    ``budget="steps"`` compares final errors (equal training points).
    ``budget="evals"`` compares each run at the last checkpoint whose residual
    evaluations (training plus sampler overhead) do not exceed the smallest
    total spent by any run on that PDE.
    """
    from scipy.stats import wilcoxon

    if budget not in ("steps", "evals"):
        raise ValueError(f"budget must be 'steps' or 'evals', got {budget!r}")
    cap: dict[str, int] = {}
    if budget == "evals":
        for run in runs:
            cap[run.pde] = min(cap.get(run.pde, run.residual_evals), run.residual_evals)

    by_key: dict[tuple[str, str], dict[int, tuple[float, float]]] = {}
    for run in runs:
        point = _at_budget(run, cap.get(run.pde))
        by_key.setdefault((run.pde, run.strategy), {})[run.seed] = point

    summaries: list[StudySummary] = []
    for (pde, strategy), seed_vals in sorted(by_key.items()):
        errors = np.array([v[0] for v in seed_vals.values()])
        baseline = by_key.get((pde, "uniform"), {})
        paired = sorted(set(seed_vals) & set(baseline))
        wins = sum(seed_vals[s][0] < baseline[s][0] for s in paired)
        p_value = float("nan")
        if strategy != "uniform" and len(paired) >= 5:
            diffs = [seed_vals[s][0] - baseline[s][0] for s in paired]
            if any(d != 0 for d in diffs):
                p_value = float(wilcoxon(diffs).pvalue)
        summaries.append(
            StudySummary(
                budget=budget,
                pde=pde,
                strategy=strategy,
                n=len(errors),
                median_rel_l2=float(np.median(errors)),
                q25_rel_l2=float(np.percentile(errors, 25)),
                q75_rel_l2=float(np.percentile(errors, 75)),
                median_time_s=float(np.median([v[1] for v in seed_vals.values()])),
                wins_vs_uniform=wins if strategy != "uniform" else 0,
                p_vs_uniform=p_value,
            )
        )
    return summaries

def solve_heat_1d(
    alpha: float = 0.1,
    frequency: float = 1.0,
    domain: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 1.0),
    t_max: float = 1.0,
    nx: int = 101,
    nt: int = 4001,
) -> FDMResult:
    """Explicit-Euler FDM solver for the 1-D heat equation on a periodic domain.

    Solves ``u_t = α·u_xx`` with initial condition ``sin(2π·f·x)`` and
    periodic boundaries. The defaults give a diffusion number
    ``r = α·dt/dx² ≈ 0.26``, about half the explicit-stability cap of 0.5.

    Args:
        alpha: Thermal diffusivity.
        frequency: Spatial frequency of the sinusoidal initial condition.
        domain: Spatial domain ``(x_min, x_max)``.
        t_max: Final time.
        nx: Number of distinct points on the periodic grid (``dx = (x_max - x_min) / nx``).
        nt: Number of time levels including ``t = 0`` (``nt - 1`` steps).

    Returns:
        :class:`FDMResult` containing the full solution grid, the analytical
        solution at ``t_max``, and L2/max error metrics.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the explicit-Euler scheme would be unstable for the
            chosen ``(nx, nt, alpha)``.
    """
    x_min, x_max = float(domain[0]), float(domain[1])
    # Periodic grid: x_max is the same point as x_min, so it is excluded.
    x = np.linspace(x_min, x_max, nx, endpoint=False, dtype=np.float64)
    t = np.linspace(0.0, t_max, nt, dtype=np.float64)
    dx = (x_max - x_min) / nx
    dt = t_max / (nt - 1)
    r = alpha * dt / (dx**2)
    if r > 0.5:
        raise ValueError(
            f"FDM heat scheme unstable: r = α·dt/dx² = {r:.3f} > 0.5. "
            f"Increase nt (currently {nt}) or decrease nx (currently {nx})."
        )

    u = np.zeros((nt, nx), dtype=np.float64)
    u[0] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * frequency * x)

    start = time.perf_counter()
    for n in range(nt - 1):
        # Periodic stencil via np.roll: u_xx ≈ (u[i+1] - 2u[i] + u[i-1]) / dx²
        lap = np.roll(u[n], -1) - 2.0 * u[n] + np.roll(u[n], 1)
        u[n + 1] = u[n] + r * lap
    wall = time.perf_counter() - start

    u_exact_final = _heat_exact(x, t_max, alpha, frequency)
    err = u[-1] - u_exact_final
    return FDMResult(
        u=u,
        u_exact_final=u_exact_final,
        x=x,
        t=t,
        l2_error=float(np.linalg.norm(err) / np.linalg.norm(u_exact_final)),
        mse=float(np.mean(err**2)),
        max_error=float(np.max(np.abs(err))),
        wall_time_s=wall,
    )

Solves u_tt = c²·u_xx with the travelling-wave initial condition u(x, 0) = sin(2πx), u_t(x, 0) = -2π·c·cos(2πx) so that the closed-form solution is the right-moving wave sin(2π(x − c·t)). def solve_wave_1d(
    c: float = 1.0,
    domain: tuple[float, float] = (0.0, 1.0),
    t_max: float = 1.0,
    nx: int = 201,
    nt: int = 4001,
) -> FDMResult:
    """Leap-frog FDM solver for the 1-D wave equation on a periodic domain.

    Solves ``u_tt = c²·u_xx`` with the travelling-wave initial condition
    ``u(x, 0) = sin(2πx)``, ``u_t(x, 0) = -2π·c·cos(2πx)`` so that the
    closed-form solution is the right-moving wave ``sin(2π(x − c·t))``. This
    is not :class:`pinnrl.pdes.wave_equation.WaveEquation`'s standing-wave
    exact solution, which starts at rest.

    Args:
        c: Wave speed.
        domain: Spatial domain ``(x_min, x_max)``.
        t_max: Final time.
        nx: Number of distinct points on the periodic grid (``dx = (x_max - x_min) / nx``).
        nt: Number of time levels including ``t = 0`` (``nt - 1`` steps).

    Returns:
        :class:`FDMResult` containing the full solution grid, the analytical
        solution at ``t_max``, and L2/max error metrics.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the leap-frog CFL condition ``c·dt/dx ≤ 1`` is violated.
    """
    x_min, x_max = float(domain[0]), float(domain[1])
    # Periodic grid: x_max is the same point as x_min, so it is excluded.
    x = np.linspace(x_min, x_max, nx, endpoint=False, dtype=np.float64)
    t = np.linspace(0.0, t_max, nt, dtype=np.float64)
    dx = (x_max - x_min) / nx
    dt = t_max / (nt - 1)
    cfl = c * dt / dx
    if cfl > 1.0:
        raise ValueError(
            f"FDM wave scheme violates CFL: c·dt/dx = {cfl:.3f} > 1. "
            f"Increase nt (currently {nt}) or decrease nx (currently {nx})."
        )

    u = np.zeros((nt, nx), dtype=np.float64)
    u[0] = np.sin(2.0 * np.pi * x)
    # First step from u_t(x, 0) = -2πc·cos(2πx). Taylor expansion:
    #   u(x, dt) ≈ u(x, 0) + dt·u_t + 0.5·dt²·u_tt   with u_tt = c²·u_xx
    u_t0 = -2.0 * np.pi * c * np.cos(2.0 * np.pi * x)
    lap0 = np.roll(u[0], -1) - 2.0 * u[0] + np.roll(u[0], 1)
    u[1] = u[0] + dt * u_t0 + 0.5 * (cfl**2) * lap0

    start = time.perf_counter()
    for n in range(1, nt - 1):
        lap = np.roll(u[n], -1) - 2.0 * u[n] + np.roll(u[n], 1)
        u[n + 1] = 2.0 * u[n] - u[n - 1] + (cfl**2) * lap
    wall = time.perf_counter() - start

    u_exact_final = _wave_exact(x, t_max, c)
    err = u[-1] - u_exact_final
    return FDMResult(
        u=u,
        u_exact_final=u_exact_final,
        x=x,
        t=t,
        l2_error=float(np.linalg.norm(err) / np.linalg.norm(u_exact_final)),
        mse=float(np.mean(err**2)),
        max_error=float(np.max(np.abs(err))),
        wall_time_s=wall,
    )

@classmethod
def from_dict(cls, cfg: dict[str, Any]) -> "TrainingConfig":
    """Build from the ``training:`` block of ``config.yaml``.

    This is the one place the YAML layout is translated into a
    ``TrainingConfig``; both :class:`Config` and ``pinnrl-train`` use it.
    ``learning_rate`` and ``weight_decay`` come from ``optimizer_config``
    (or the top level); the scheduler from ``scheduler_type``,
    ``warmup_epochs`` and ``reduce_lr_params``; a legacy ``pde`` key in
    ``loss_weights`` is renamed to ``residual``. Missing keys fall back to
    defaults. Float fields are coerced with ``float()`` because YAML 1.1
    reads ``1e-7`` (no decimal point) as a string.
    """
    optimizer_cfg = cfg.get("optimizer_config", {})
    early_stopping = cfg.get("early_stopping", {})
    reduce_lr = cfg.get("reduce_lr_params", {})
    adaptive = cfg.get("adaptive_weights", {})
    lbfgs = cfg.get("lbfgs", {})

    loss_weights = cfg.get("loss_weights")
    if loss_weights is not None and "pde" in loss_weights:
        loss_weights = dict(loss_weights)
        loss_weights["residual"] = loss_weights.pop("pde")

    return cls(
        num_epochs=cfg.get("num_epochs", 10000),
        batch_size=cfg.get("batch_size", 128),
        num_collocation_points=cfg.get("num_collocation_points", 1000),
        num_boundary_points=cfg.get("num_boundary_points", 100),
        num_initial_points=cfg.get("num_initial_points", 100),
        learning_rate=float(
            optimizer_cfg.get("learning_rate", cfg.get("learning_rate", 0.001))
        ),
        weight_decay=float(optimizer_cfg.get("weight_decay", cfg.get("weight_decay", 0.0001))),
        gradient_clipping=float(cfg.get("gradient_clipping", 1.0)),
        early_stopping=EarlyStoppingConfig(
            enabled=early_stopping.get("enabled", True),
            patience=early_stopping.get("patience", 100),
            min_delta=float(early_stopping.get("min_delta", 1e-4)),
        ),
        learning_rate_scheduler=LearningRateSchedulerConfig(
            type=cfg.get("scheduler_type", "cosine"),
            warmup_epochs=cfg.get("warmup_epochs", 0),
            min_lr=float(reduce_lr.get("min_lr", 1e-6)),
            factor=float(reduce_lr.get("factor", 0.5)),
            patience=reduce_lr.get("patience", 50),
        ),
        collocation_distribution=cfg.get("collocation_distribution", "uniform"),
        adaptive_weights=AdaptiveWeightsConfig(
            enabled=adaptive.get("enabled", False),
            strategy=adaptive.get("strategy", "rbw"),
            alpha=float(adaptive.get("alpha", 0.9)),
            eps=float(adaptive.get("eps", 1e-5)),
            initial_weights=adaptive.get("initial_weights"),
        ),
        loss_weights=loss_weights,
        optimizer=cfg.get("optimizer", "adam"),
        adam_lbfgs_switch_ratio=float(cfg.get("adam_lbfgs_switch_ratio", 0.7)),
        lbfgs=LBFGSConfig(
            **{k: _lbfgs_value(k, v) for k, v in lbfgs.items() if k in _LBFGS_FIELDS}
        ),
        mode=cfg.get("mode", "forward"),
        loss_function=cfg.get("loss_function", "mse"),
        huber_delta=float(cfg.get("huber_delta", 1.0)),
        validation_frequency=int(cfg.get("validation_frequency", 10)),
    )

def __init__(
    self,
    input_dim: int,
    hidden_dim: int,
    output_dim: int,
    num_layers: int,
    activation: str,
    fourier_features: int = 0,
    fourier_scale: float = 1.0,
    dropout: float = 0.0,
    layer_norm: bool = False,
    architecture: str = "feedforward",
):
    self.input_dim = input_dim
    self.hidden_dim = hidden_dim
    self.output_dim = output_dim
    self.num_layers = num_layers
    self.activation = activation
    self.fourier_features = fourier_features
    self.fourier_scale = fourier_scale
    self.dropout = dropout
    self.layer_norm = layer_norm
    self.architecture = architecture

    # Configure hidden_dims as a list based on hidden_dim when not explicitly set
    self.hidden_dims = [hidden_dim] * num_layers

    # For ResNet and FNO, set num_blocks to be the same as num_layers
    if architecture in ("resnet", "fno"):
        self.num_blocks = num_layers

@classmethod
def from_architecture(
    cls,
    architecture: str,
    arch_cfg: dict[str, Any],
    input_dim: int,
    output_dim: int,
) -> "ModelConfig":
    """Build from one entry of the ``architectures:`` block of ``config.yaml``.

    ``hidden_dim`` and ``num_layers`` default to the first width and the
    length of ``hidden_dims`` when only the list is given (else 128 and 4);
    ``activation`` defaults to ``tanh``. Architecture extras
    (``omega_0``, ``modes``, ...) are copied when present.
    """
    hidden_dims = arch_cfg.get("hidden_dims")
    model = cls(
        input_dim=input_dim,
        hidden_dim=arch_cfg.get("hidden_dim", hidden_dims[0] if hidden_dims else 128),
        output_dim=output_dim,
        num_layers=arch_cfg.get("num_layers", len(hidden_dims) if hidden_dims else 4),
        activation=arch_cfg.get("activation", "tanh"),
        fourier_features=architecture == "fourier",
        fourier_scale=arch_cfg.get("scale", 1.0),
        dropout=arch_cfg.get("dropout", 0.0),
        layer_norm=arch_cfg.get("layer_norm", False),
        architecture=architecture,
    )
    for key in _ARCHITECTURE_EXTRAS:
        if key in arch_cfg:
            setattr(model, key, arch_cfg[key])
    return model

def resolve_device(name: str) -> torch.device:
    """Return ``torch.device(name)`` if that backend is available, else CPU.

    Only ``"cuda"`` and ``"mps"`` are probed; any other name resolves to CPU,
    so a config written on one machine still runs on another.
    """
    if name == "cuda" and torch.cuda.is_available():
        return torch.device("cuda")
    if name == "mps" and torch.backends.mps.is_available():
        return torch.device("mps")
    return torch.device("cpu")

def mlp_jets(
    linears: Sequence[torch.nn.Linear],
    x: torch.Tensor,
    first: Sequence[int] = (),
    second: Sequence[int] = (),
    norms: Sequence[torch.nn.LayerNorm] = (),
) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, dict[int, torch.Tensor], dict[int, torch.Tensor]]:
    """Value and derivatives of a tanh MLP at ``x`` through the compiled kernel.

    Args:
        linears: The ``Linear`` layers in order (``tanh`` between them).
        x: Inputs, ``(N, d)``, float32 on the CPU; treated as data (no gradient flows to it).
        first: Input columns to differentiate once.
        second: Input columns to differentiate twice (each is added to ``first`` if missing).
        norms: The ``LayerNorm`` after each hidden ``Linear`` (before its ``tanh``), or none.

    Returns:
        ``(u, du, d2u)``: the output ``(N, k)``, ``{column: du/dx_column}`` and
        ``{column: d2u/dx_column^2}``, all differentiable with respect to the weights.

    Raises:
        RuntimeError: When the kernel is not available (see :func:`unavailable_reason`) or the
            input is not float32 on the CPU.
        ValueError: When ``norms`` does not have one entry per hidden layer.
    """
    if not available():
        raise RuntimeError(unavailable_reason())
    if x.dtype != torch.float32 or x.device.type != "cpu":
        raise RuntimeError("the native kernel needs float32 inputs on the CPU")
    if norms and len(norms) != len(linears) - 1:
        raise ValueError("norms needs one LayerNorm per hidden layer")
    first_cols = list(dict.fromkeys([*first, *second]))
    parent = [first_cols.index(c) for c in second]
    params: list[torch.Tensor] = []
    for lin in linears:
        params += [lin.weight, lin.bias]
    for norm in norms:
        params += [norm.weight, norm.bias]
    eps = float(norms[0].eps) if norms else 0.0
    out = _Jets.apply(x, tuple(first_cols), tuple(parent), len(linears), eps, *params)
    n = x.shape[0]
    u = out[:n]
    du = {c: out[(1 + i) * n : (2 + i) * n] for i, c in enumerate(first_cols)}
    d2u = {
        c: out[(1 + len(first_cols) + j) * n : (2 + len(first_cols) + j) * n]
        for j, c in enumerate(second)
    }
    return u, du, d2u

def __init__(self, config: "Config", device=None, **kwargs):
    """Initialize the PINN model.

    Args:
        config: Configuration object with ``model`` and ``device``;
            ``config.model.device`` is set to the chosen device.
        device: Optional device to override config device
        **kwargs: Ignored.
    """
    # Store configuration
    self.config = config

    # Use provided device or get from config
    self.device = device if device is not None else config.device

    # Override device in config with the determined device
    config_with_device = config.model
    config_with_device.device = self.device

    # BaseNetwork reads the ModelConfig through its dict-like .get
    super().__init__(config_with_device)

    # Store architecture type
    self.architecture = config.model.architecture
    self.architecture_name = config.model.architecture  # More accessible name for metadata

    # Create model based on architecture
    if self.architecture == "fourier":
        self.model: BaseNetwork = FourierNetwork(config_with_device)
    elif self.architecture == "resnet":
        # Create a specific configuration dictionary for ResNet
        resnet_config = {
            "input_dim": config.model.input_dim,
            "hidden_dim": config.model.hidden_dim,
            "output_dim": config.model.output_dim,
            "activation": config.model.activation,
            "dropout": config.model.dropout,
            "device": self.device,
        }

        # Make sure num_blocks is defined, using num_layers as fallback
        if hasattr(config.model, "num_blocks") and config.model.num_blocks is not None:
            resnet_config["num_blocks"] = config.model.num_blocks
        else:
            resnet_config["num_blocks"] = config.model.num_layers

        # Add hidden_dims if defined
        if hasattr(config.model, "hidden_dims") and config.model.hidden_dims is not None:
            resnet_config["hidden_dims"] = config.model.hidden_dims

        self.model = ResNet(resnet_config)
    elif self.architecture == "siren":
        self.model = SIREN(config_with_device)
    elif self.architecture == "attention":
        self.model = AttentionNetwork(config_with_device)
    elif self.architecture == "autoencoder":
        self.model = AutoEncoder(config_with_device)
    elif self.architecture == "fno":
        fno_config = {
            "input_dim": config.model.input_dim,
            "hidden_dim": config.model.hidden_dim,
            "output_dim": config.model.output_dim,
            "num_blocks": getattr(config.model, "num_blocks", None) or config.model.num_layers,
            "modes": config.model.get("modes", 16),
            "activation": config.model.activation,
            "device": self.device,
        }
        self.model = FNONetwork(fno_config)
    else:  # Default to feedforward
        self.model = FeedForwardNetwork(config_with_device)

    # Non-dimensionalization: an affine map of the inputs to [-1, 1] and of the
    # outputs to their physical scale, kept as buffers so a checkpoint carries them.
    bounds = config.model.get("input_bounds")
    scale = config.model.get("output_scale")
    offset = config.model.get("output_offset")
    self.scaled = bounds is not None or scale is not None or offset is not None
    if bounds is not None:
        b = torch.as_tensor(bounds, dtype=torch.float32)
        if b.shape != (config.model.input_dim, 2):
            raise ValueError(
                f"input_bounds needs one (lo, hi) pair per input, {config.model.input_dim}; got {b.shape}"
            )
        self.register_buffer("_in_lo", b[:, 0])
        self.register_buffer("_in_span", (b[:, 1] - b[:, 0]).clamp_min(1e-12))
    else:
        self._in_lo = None
    k = config.model.output_dim
    self.register_buffer(
        "_out_scale",
        torch.as_tensor(scale if scale is not None else [1.0] * k, dtype=torch.float32).reshape(
            1, k
        ),
    )
    self.register_buffer(
        "_out_offset",
        torch.as_tensor(
            offset if offset is not None else [0.0] * k, dtype=torch.float32
        ).reshape(1, k),
    )

    # Explicitly move the model to the specified device
    self.model = self.model.to(self.device)
    self.to(self.device)
    #: Evaluate inputs that do not require grad through the compiled kernel
    #: (:mod:`pinnrl.native`) when it applies; set by ``build_trainer(derivatives="native")``.
    self.native_values = False

Forward pass of the model.

With input_bounds the inputs are mapped to [-1, 1] first; with output_scale / output_offset the network's output is returned as offset + scale * net(x). Without them this is self.model(x).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default x

required

Type Description

Source code in pinnrl/neural_networks/__init__.py 
def forward(self, x):
    """Forward pass of the model.

    With ``input_bounds`` the inputs are mapped to ``[-1, 1]`` first; with
    ``output_scale`` / ``output_offset`` the network's output is returned
    as ``offset + scale * net(x)``. Without them this is ``self.model(x)``.

    Args:
        x: Input tensor of shape (batch_size, input_dim)

    Returns:
        Output tensor of shape (batch_size, output_dim)
    """
    if (
        self.native_values
        and isinstance(x, torch.Tensor)
        and not x.requires_grad
        and x.dim() == 2
    ):
        got = self.jets(x)  # the compiled kernel, for points nothing is differentiated at
        if got is not None:
            return got[0]
    if not self.scaled:
        return self.model(x)
    if self._in_lo is not None:
        x = 2.0 * (x - self._in_lo) / self._in_span - 1.0
    return self._out_offset + self._out_scale * self.model(x)

docs.text:
jets(x, first=(), second=())

Value and derivatives by the compiled kernel, or None when it does not apply.

(u, du, d2u) with du[c] the derivative of every output with respect to input column c (for c in first and second) and d2u[c] the pure second derivative (c in second), each (N, output_dim) and differentiable with respect to the weights once. The non-dimensionalization of the inputs and outputs is applied. The kernel covers a feed-forward stack of Linear and tanh, with or without layer normalization, in float32 on the CPU (:mod:pinnrl.native); for any other network, on another device, or where the kernel cannot be built, this returns None and the caller differentiates by autograd.

Source code in pinnrl/neural_networks/__init__.py 
def jets(self, x, first=(), second=()):
    """Value and derivatives by the compiled kernel, or ``None`` when it does not apply.

    ``(u, du, d2u)`` with ``du[c]`` the derivative of every output with
    respect to input column ``c`` (for ``c`` in ``first`` and ``second``)
    and ``d2u[c]`` the pure second derivative (``c`` in ``second``), each
    ``(N, output_dim)`` and differentiable with respect to the weights
    once. The non-dimensionalization of the inputs and outputs is applied.
    The kernel covers a feed-forward stack of ``Linear`` and ``tanh``, with
    or without layer normalization, in float32 on the CPU (:mod:`pinnrl.native`); for any other network, on
    another device, or where the kernel cannot be built, this returns
    ``None`` and the caller differentiates by autograd.
    """
    from pinnrl import native

    layers = getattr(self.model, "layers", None)
    if not isinstance(self.model, FeedForwardNetwork) or layers is None:
        return None
    if x.device.type != "cpu" or x.dtype != torch.float32 or not native.available():
        return None
    stack = native.supported_stack(list(layers))
    if stack is None or stack[0][0].weight.dtype != torch.float32:
        return None
    linears, norms = stack
    z, slope = x, None
    if self.scaled and self._in_lo is not None:
        z = 2.0 * (x - self._in_lo) / self._in_span - 1.0
        slope = 2.0 / self._in_span  # dz/dx per input column
    u, du, d2u = native.mlp_jets(linears, z, first, second, norms)
    if self.scaled:
        u = self._out_offset + self._out_scale * u
        du = {c: self._out_scale * g for c, g in du.items()}
        d2u = {c: self._out_scale * g for c, g in d2u.items()}
    if slope is not None:
        du = {c: g * slope[c] for c, g in du.items()}
        d2u = {c: g * slope[c] ** 2 for c, g in d2u.items()}
    return u, du, d2u

docs.title: ExactLayerNorm
docs.text:
Bases: LayerNorm

Layer normalization over the last dimension, written out in elementary operations.

torch.nn.LayerNorm returns the right values and the right first and second derivatives, but its third-order derivative is wrong (PyTorch 2.10, checked against finite differences): the weight gradient of a loss that contains second derivatives of the network with respect to its inputs, which is every PINN residual with a u_xx, comes out 2 to 3 % off in norm on a 4 x 64 network. Composed of elementary operations the same function differentiates correctly to any order. The parameters and their names are those of nn.LayerNorm, so checkpoints load either way.

weight * (x - mean) / sqrt(var + eps) + bias over the last dimension.

Source code in pinnrl/neural_networks/base_network.py 
def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """``weight * (x - mean) / sqrt(var + eps) + bias`` over the last dimension."""
    if len(self.normalized_shape) != 1:
        return super().forward(x)
    c = x - x.mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True)
    y = c * torch.rsqrt(c.square().mean(dim=-1, keepdim=True) + self.eps)
    if not self.elementwise_affine:
        return y
    if self.bias is None:
        return y * self.weight
    return torch.addcmul(self.bias, self.weight, y)  # as fast as the built-in under autograd

def __init__(self, config: NetworkConfig) -> None:
    """Initialize the feed-forward network.

    Args:
        config: Network configuration dictionary containing:
            - input_dim: Input dimension
            - hidden_dims: List of hidden layer dimensions
            - output_dim: Output dimension
            - activation: Activation function name ('relu', 'tanh', etc.; default 'relu')
            - dropout: Dropout rate (default 0.1)
            - layer_norm: Whether to use layer normalization (default True)
            - device: Device to place the model on
    """
    super().__init__(config)
    self.input_dim = config["input_dim"]
    self.hidden_dims = config["hidden_dims"]
    self.output_dim = config["output_dim"]
    self.dropout_rate = config.get("dropout", 0.1)
    self.use_layer_norm = config.get("layer_norm", True)
    self.device = config.get("device", torch.device("cpu"))

    # Get activation function name for per-layer instantiation
    activation_name = config.get("activation", "relu")

    # Build layers
    layers: list[nn.Module] = []
    prev_dim = self.input_dim

    for hidden_dim in self.hidden_dims:
        layers.append(nn.Linear(prev_dim, hidden_dim))
        if self.use_layer_norm:
            layers.append(ExactLayerNorm(hidden_dim))
        # A fresh activation module per layer
        layers.append(self._get_activation_module(activation_name))
        if self.dropout_rate > 0.0:
            layers.append(nn.Dropout(self.dropout_rate))
        prev_dim = hidden_dim

    # Output layer
    layers.append(nn.Linear(prev_dim, self.output_dim))

    self.layers = nn.Sequential(*layers)

    # Move model to device
    self.to(self.device)

def __init__(self, config: NetworkConfig) -> None:
    """Initialize the ResNet architecture.

    Args:
        config: Network configuration dictionary containing:
            - input_dim: Input dimension
            - hidden_dim: Hidden layer dimension (else ``hidden_dims[0]``, else 124)
            - num_blocks: Number of ResNetBlock components (else ``num_layers``, else 4)
            - output_dim: Output dimension
            - activation: Activation function name (default ``relu``)
            - dropout: Dropout rate (default 0.1)
    """
    super().__init__(config)
    self.input_dim = config["input_dim"]

    # Support both hidden_dim (scalar) and hidden_dims (list)
    if "hidden_dim" in config:
        self.hidden_dim = config["hidden_dim"]
    elif (
        "hidden_dims" in config
        and isinstance(config["hidden_dims"], list)
        and len(config["hidden_dims"]) > 0
    ):
        self.hidden_dim = config["hidden_dims"][0]
    else:
        self.hidden_dim = 124  # Default value if nothing is specified

    # Support both num_blocks and num_layers
    if "num_blocks" in config:
        self.num_blocks = config["num_blocks"]
    elif "num_layers" in config:
        self.num_blocks = config["num_layers"]
    else:
        self.num_blocks = 4  # Default value if nothing is specified

    self.output_dim = config["output_dim"]
    activation_name = config.get("activation", "relu")
    self.activation_fn = self._get_activation_module(activation_name)
    self.dropout = config.get("dropout", 0.1)

    # Build the ResNet architecture
    self.input_layer = nn.Linear(self.input_dim, self.hidden_dim)
    # Stack multiple ResNetBlock components
    self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(
        [
            ResNetBlock(
                self.hidden_dim,
                self.hidden_dim,
                config.get("activation", "relu"),
                self.dropout,
            )
            for _ in range(self.num_blocks)
        ]
    )
    self.output_layer = nn.Linear(self.hidden_dim, self.output_dim)

def __init__(
    self,
    in_dim: int,
    hidden_dim: int,
    activation: str = "relu",
    dropout: float = 0.1,
):
    """Initialize a single residual block component.

    Args:
        in_dim: Input dimension
        hidden_dim: Hidden dimension
        activation: Activation function name
        dropout: Dropout rate
    """
    super().__init__()

    # Get activation function
    if activation == "relu":
        self.activation_fn: nn.Module = nn.ReLU()
    elif activation == "leaky_relu":
        self.activation_fn = nn.LeakyReLU()
    elif activation == "tanh":
        self.activation_fn = nn.Tanh()
    elif activation == "sigmoid":
        self.activation_fn = nn.Sigmoid()
    elif activation == "gelu":
        self.activation_fn = nn.GELU()
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"Unsupported activation: {activation}")

    # Build the residual block
    self.layers = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Linear(in_dim, hidden_dim),
        ExactLayerNorm(hidden_dim),
        self.activation_fn,
        nn.Dropout(dropout),
        nn.Linear(hidden_dim, in_dim),
        ExactLayerNorm(in_dim),
        nn.Dropout(dropout),
    )

def initialize_weights(self) -> None:
    """Draw ``W ~ U(-sqrt(6 / in) / omega_0, sqrt(6 / in) / omega_0)``.

    This is the SIREN hidden-layer rule; it is used for every layer,
    including the first (the paper's first-layer ``U(-1/in, 1/in)`` is not
    applied). Biases keep PyTorch's default ``nn.Linear`` initialization.
    """
    with torch.no_grad():
        self.linear.weight.uniform_(
            -np.sqrt(6 / self.linear.in_features) / self.omega_0,
            np.sqrt(6 / self.linear.in_features) / self.omega_0,
        )

def __init__(self, config: NetworkConfig) -> None:
    """Initialize the network.

    Args:
        config: Network configuration dictionary containing:
            - input_dim: Input dimension
            - mapping_size: Size of the Fourier feature mapping (default 32)
            - hidden_dims: Width of each hidden layer (one layer per entry,
              like the feedforward network); falls back to
              ``[hidden_dim] * num_layers`` (``num_layers`` default 4)
            - output_dim: Output dimension
            - activation: Activation function name (default ``relu``)
            - scale: Standard deviation of ``B`` (default 10.0)
    """
    super().__init__(config)
    self.input_dim = config["input_dim"]
    self.mapping_size = config.get("mapping_size", 32)  # Default mapping size
    self.hidden_dims = list(
        config.get("hidden_dims") or [config["hidden_dim"]] * config.get("num_layers", 4)
    )
    self.output_dim = config["output_dim"]
    activation_name = config.get("activation", "relu")
    self.activation_fn = self._get_activation_module(activation_name)
    self.scale = config.get("scale", 10.0)

    # Build layers
    self.fourier = FourierFeatures(
        self.input_dim, self.mapping_size, self.scale, device=self.device
    )
    self.layers = nn.ModuleList()
    prev_dim = 2 * self.mapping_size  # Sine and cosine features

    # One hidden layer per width, then the output layer
    for width in self.hidden_dims:
        self.layers.append(nn.Linear(prev_dim, width))
        prev_dim = width

    # Add output layer
    self.layers.append(nn.Linear(prev_dim, self.output_dim))

    # Move all layers to device
    self.to(self.device)

def __init__(
    self,
    input_dim: int,
    mapping_size: int,
    scale: float = 10.0,
    device: torch.device | None = None,
):
    """Initialize Fourier features.

    Args:
        input_dim: Input dimension
        mapping_size: Number of frequencies (output has ``2 * mapping_size`` features)
        scale: Standard deviation of the entries of ``B``
        device: Device to place the features on (default: MPS if available, else CPU)
    """
    super().__init__()
    self.input_dim = input_dim
    self.mapping_size = mapping_size
    self.scale = scale
    self.device = device or torch.device("mps" if torch.backends.mps.is_available() else "cpu")

    # Fixed random frequencies B ~ N(0, scale^2)
    self.register_buffer("B", torch.randn(input_dim, mapping_size, device=self.device) * scale)

    # Pre-compute output dimension
    self.output_dim = mapping_size * 2

Fourier Neural Operator network for point-wise PINN training.

Architecture

Input(input_dim) -> Lift(Linear-GELU-Linear, hidden_dim) -> [FNOBlock(hidden_dim)] x num_blocks -> Project(Linear-GELU-Linear, output_dim)

Config keys: input_dim, output_dim, hidden_dim (default 128), num_blocks (default 4), modes (default 16) and activation of the blocks (default gelu).

def __init__(self, config: NetworkConfig) -> None:
    super().__init__(config)

    self.input_dim = config["input_dim"]
    self.output_dim = config["output_dim"]
    self.hidden_dim = config.get("hidden_dim", 128)
    self.num_blocks = config.get("num_blocks", 4)
    self.modes = config.get("modes", 16)
    activation = config.get("activation", "gelu")

    # Lifting layer: project (x, t) to higher-dimensional channel space
    self.lift = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Linear(self.input_dim, self.hidden_dim),
        nn.GELU(),
        nn.Linear(self.hidden_dim, self.hidden_dim),
    )

    # Spectral convolution blocks
    self.blocks = nn.ModuleList(
        [FNOBlock(self.hidden_dim, self.modes, activation) for _ in range(self.num_blocks)]
    )

    # Projection layers: channel space -> solution
    self.project = nn.Sequential(
        nn.Linear(self.hidden_dim, self.hidden_dim),
        nn.GELU(),
        nn.Linear(self.hidden_dim, self.output_dim),
    )

    self.to(self.device)

def forward(self, x: InputType) -> OutputType:
    """Map ``(x, t)`` points to the solution through the spectral blocks."""
    x = self._prepare_input(x)

    # Lift to channel space
    h = self.lift(x)

    for block in self.blocks:
        h = block(h)

    # Project to output
    return self.project(h)

docs.title: SpectralConv1d
docs.text:
SpectralConv1d(channels, modes)

Bases: Module

1D spectral convolution layer operating in Fourier space.

Treats the feature/channel dimension as a 1D signal::

X = rfft(x)                                    # (batch, channels // 2 + 1)
Y[:, n] = sum_{m < M} X[:, m] * W[m, n]        # n < M; Y = 0 for n >= M
y = irfft(Y, n=channels)

with M = min(modes, channels // 2 + 1) and W a learnable complex (M, M) matrix (initialised N(0, 1) / (channels * M) per real and imaginary part), so the kept modes are mixed, not scaled one by one.

Source code in pinnrl/neural_networks/fno.py 
def __init__(self, channels: int, modes: int):
    super().__init__()
    self.channels = channels
    self.modes = min(modes, channels // 2 + 1)

    # Learnable complex weights: (modes, modes) in complex = (modes, modes, 2) real
    scale = 1.0 / (channels * self.modes)
    self.weights = nn.Parameter(scale * torch.randn(self.modes, self.modes, 2))

def forward(self, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Apply spectral convolution along the feature dimension.

    Args:
        x: (batch, channels) tensor

    Returns:
        (batch, channels) tensor
    """
    # FFT along feature dimension
    x_ft = torch.fft.rfft(x, dim=-1)  # (batch, channels//2+1) complex

    # Truncate to kept modes
    modes = self.modes
    x_ft_trunc = x_ft[:, :modes]  # (batch, modes)

    # Complex weight multiplication: (batch, modes) x (modes, modes) -> (batch, modes)
    w = torch.view_as_complex(self.weights)  # (modes, modes)
    out_ft = torch.einsum("bm,mn->bn", x_ft_trunc, w)

    # Pad back to full frequency size and IFFT
    out_full = torch.zeros_like(x_ft)
    out_full[:, :modes] = out_ft
    return torch.fft.irfft(out_full, n=self.channels, dim=-1)

def __init__(self, config: NetworkConfig) -> None:
    """Initialize the network.

    Args:
        config: Network configuration dictionary containing:
            - input_dim: Input dimension
            - hidden_dim: Hidden dimension
            - output_dim: Output dimension
            - num_layers: Number of SelfAttention + FeedForwardBlock pairs
            - num_heads: Number of attention heads (must divide hidden_dim)
            - dropout: Dropout rate
            - activation: Activation after the input projection only
    """
    super().__init__(config)
    self.input_dim = config["input_dim"]
    self.hidden_dim = config["hidden_dim"]
    self.output_dim = config["output_dim"]
    self.num_layers = config.get("num_layers", 4)
    self.num_heads = config.get("num_heads", 4)
    self.dropout = config.get("dropout", 0.1)
    activation_name = config.get("activation", "gelu")
    self.activation_fn = self._get_activation_module(activation_name)

    # Input projection
    self.input_proj = nn.Linear(self.input_dim, self.hidden_dim)

    # Attention layers
    self.layers = nn.ModuleList()
    for _ in range(self.num_layers):
        self.layers.append(
            nn.ModuleList(
                [
                    SelfAttention(self.hidden_dim, self.num_heads, self.dropout),
                    FeedForwardBlock(self.hidden_dim, dropout=self.dropout),
                ]
            )
        )

    # Output projection
    self.output_proj = nn.Linear(self.hidden_dim, self.output_dim)

    # Initialize weights
    self.apply(self._init_weights)

def __init__(self, dim: int, heads: int = 4, dropout: float = 0.1) -> None:
    """Initialize the attention layer.

    Args:
        dim: Input dimension
        heads: Number of attention heads
        dropout: Dropout rate
    """
    super().__init__()
    self.dim = dim
    self.heads = heads
    self.head_dim = dim // heads
    assert self.head_dim * heads == dim, "Dimension must be divisible by heads"

    self.query = nn.Linear(dim, dim)
    self.key = nn.Linear(dim, dim)
    self.value = nn.Linear(dim, dim)
    self.proj = nn.Linear(dim, dim)
    self.dropout = nn.Dropout(dropout)
    self.scale = self.head_dim**-0.5
    self.layer_norm = ExactLayerNorm(dim)

def forward(self, x: Tensor) -> Tensor:
    """Forward pass of the layer.

    Args:
        x: Input tensor of shape (batch_size, dim)

    Returns:
        Output tensor of shape (batch_size, dim)
    """
    residual = x
    batch_size = x.shape[0]

    # Use unsqueeze to add sequence length dimension of 1
    # Shape: (batch_size, 1, dim)
    x = x.unsqueeze(1)

    # Linear projections
    q = self.query(x).view(batch_size, 1, self.heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
    k = self.key(x).view(batch_size, 1, self.heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)
    v = self.value(x).view(batch_size, 1, self.heads, self.head_dim).transpose(1, 2)

    # Attention
    scores = torch.matmul(q, k.transpose(-2, -1)) * self.scale
    attn = F.softmax(scores, dim=-1)
    attn = self.dropout(attn)

    # Apply attention to values
    out = torch.matmul(attn, v)
    out = out.transpose(1, 2).contiguous().view(batch_size, 1, self.dim)
    out = self.proj(out).squeeze(1)  # Remove sequence dimension

    # Add residual connection and apply layer norm
    out = self.layer_norm(out + residual)

    return out

            - latent_dim: Latent space dimension
            - hidden_dims: Encoder hidden widths; the decoder uses them reversed
            - output_dim: Output dimension (default 1)
            - activation: Activation function name
            - dropout: Dropout rate (default 0.0)
            - layer_norm: LayerNorm after each hidden linear layer (default True)
    """
    super().__init__(config)
    self.input_dim = config["input_dim"]
    self.latent_dim = config.get("latent_dim", 16)
    self.hidden_dims = config.get("hidden_dims", [32, 64])
    activation_name = config.get("activation", "relu")
    self.dropout_rate = config.get("dropout", 0.0)
    self.use_layer_norm = config.get("layer_norm", True)

    self.output_dim = config.get("output_dim", 1)

    # Encoder maps input -> latent; the decoder maps latent -> output_dim
    # for PINN function approximation.
    self.encoder = nn.ModuleList()
    prev_dim = self.input_dim
    for hidden_dim in self.hidden_dims:
        self.encoder.append(nn.Linear(prev_dim, hidden_dim))
        if self.use_layer_norm:
            self.encoder.append(ExactLayerNorm(hidden_dim))
        self.encoder.append(self._get_activation_module(activation_name))
        if self.dropout_rate > 0.0:
            self.encoder.append(nn.Dropout(self.dropout_rate))
        prev_dim = hidden_dim
    self.encoder.append(nn.Linear(prev_dim, self.latent_dim))

    # Decoder: latent -> output_dim (solution value)
    self.decoder = nn.ModuleList()
    prev_dim = self.latent_dim
    for hidden_dim in reversed(self.hidden_dims):
        self.decoder.append(nn.Linear(prev_dim, hidden_dim))
        if self.use_layer_norm:
            self.decoder.append(ExactLayerNorm(hidden_dim))
        self.decoder.append(self._get_activation_module(activation_name))
        if self.dropout_rate > 0.0:
            self.decoder.append(nn.Dropout(self.dropout_rate))
        prev_dim = hidden_dim
    self.decoder.append(nn.Linear(prev_dim, self.output_dim))

def encode(self, x: InputType) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Encode input to latent space.

    Args:

def forward(self, x: InputType) -> OutputType:
    """Forward pass of the network.

    Args:
        x: Input tensor or array
