Bases: PDEBase

A PDE, ODE or system defined by its residual expressions.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default equations Equations

One expression ("u_t - alpha*u_xx"), a list of them for a system (one per field), or a callable residual(f, p) taking a :class:Fields accessor and the parameter dict and returning a tensor (N, k) or a sequence of (N, 1) tensors.

required domain Mapping[str, Sequence[float]]

{coordinate: (lo, hi)}. Spatial coordinates come first in the network input, in the order given; "t" is the time axis. A domain with only "t" is an ODE (the network gets a dummy spatial input it learns to ignore); one without "t" is a steady problem (no initial condition; t is fixed at 0).

required fields Sequence[str]

Output names, default ("u",).

('u',) parameters Mapping[str, float] | None

Name to value for every parameter the expressions use.

None initial_condition Any

u(x, t0): an expression in the spatial coordinates (and parameters), a list or {field: expression} for systems, or a callable u0(x) -> (N, k). None means no initial term.

None initial_velocity Any

u_t(x, t0) in the same forms, used when an equation is second order in time (default 0).

None boundary_conditions Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]] | None

As for :class:PDEBase (dirichlet, neumann, periodic), applied to every field; or, for a system, {field: {kind: options}} with its own conditions per field (a field left out has none).

None exact_solution Any

u(x, t) in the same forms as the initial condition (expressions may use t), or a callable u(x, t) -> (N, k); enables :meth:validate.

None name str

Display name for runs and the dashboard.

'Custom PDE' trainable_parameters Sequence[str]

Parameters to identify in inverse mode.

() parameter_initial_guesses Mapping[str, float] | None

Their starting values.

None inputs Mapping[str, Any] | None

Measured inputs, {name: TimeSeries | spec} (see :class:~pinnrl.pdes.inputs.TimeSeries): a signal of t that the equations and boundary values may use by name, read at the time of each point. Boundary values (dirichlet value / left / right, neumann value) may also be expressions in the coordinates, parameters and inputs.

None parametric Mapping[str, Sequence[float]] | None

{parameter: (lo, hi)}: parameters the network takes as extra inputs, sampled uniformly over the range with the collocation points, so one training gives a surrogate u(x, t; theta) over the whole prior range (a parametric surrogate, K45). They are used in the expressions like coordinates; boundary conditions are not applied on their faces. :meth:surrogate_misfit evaluates the data misfit of the trained surrogate for a batch of parameter values, the forward model a swarm or a sampler needs.

None sensors Sequence[Sensor | Mapping[str, Any]] | None

Observation operators (see :mod:pinnrl.pdes.sensors): :class:~pinnrl.pdes.sensors.PointSensor, :class:~pinnrl.pdes.sensors.BoundarySensor, :class:~pinnrl.pdes.sensors.IntegralSensor or their specs. Each sensor's records enter the data loss as its own weighted term; :meth:observe fills them from the exact solution.

None scales Mapping[str, float | Sequence[float]] | None

{field: scale} or {field: (offset, scale)}, the magnitude (and typical value) of each field in its physical units, e.g. {"T": (300.0, 50.0)} for a temperature around 300 K varying by tens of kelvin. With build_trainer(normalize=True) the network predicts offset + scale * net(x̂) over inputs mapped to [-1, 1], so a problem written in metres, seconds and kelvin trains like one on the unit square.

None field_weights Mapping[str, float] | None

{field: weight} for systems: the field's residual, initial and boundary errors enter the loss multiplied by this weight (default 1), so a slow or small component can be given more say than its scale would.

None unknown_functions Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any] | UnknownFunction] | None

Field-valued unknowns, {name: spec} with the keys of :class:~pinnrl.pdes.unknowns.UnknownFunction (inputs, hidden, positive, bounds, monotone, initial, truth, ...) or ready-built instances. The name is used in the expressions like a parameter ("u_t - alpha*u_xx", with alpha_x for its derivative). Their weights are trained in inverse mode; the truth serves synthetic data and grading.

None observation_data Mapping[str, Any] | None

Observations for the data term (see :class:PDEConfig).

A TrainingConfig or dict of training options.

None device device | str | None

Torch device.

None time_order int | None

Override for the order in time (derived from the expressions when they are text; needed for a callable residual that is second order in time).

Default architecture for :meth:build_trainer.

def __init__(
    self,
    equations: Equations,
    *,
    domain: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]],
    fields: Sequence[str] = ("u",),
    parameters: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    initial_condition: Any = None,
    initial_velocity: Any = None,
    boundary_conditions: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any]] | None = None,
    exact_solution: Any = None,
    name: str = "Custom PDE",
    trainable_parameters: Sequence[str] = (),
    parameter_initial_guesses: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    unknown_functions: Mapping[str, Mapping[str, Any] | UnknownFunction] | None = None,
    field_weights: Mapping[str, float] | None = None,
    scales: Mapping[str, float | Sequence[float]] | None = None,
    inputs: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    sensors: Sequence[Sensor | Mapping[str, Any]] | None = None,
    parametric: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]] | None = None,
    observation_data: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    training: Any = None,
    device: torch.device | str | None = None,
    time_order: int | None = None,
    architecture: str = "fourier",
    **_ignored: Any,
):
    """Build the problem; see the class docstring for the arguments."""
    self.fields = tuple(fields)
    if not self.fields:
        raise ValueError("fields must name at least one network output")
    domain = {str(k): (float(v[0]), float(v[1])) for k, v in domain.items()}
    self.parametric = tuple(str(k) for k in (parametric or {}))
    for pname, rng in dict(parametric or {}).items():
        if pname in domain or pname in (parameters or {}):
            raise ValueError(f"parametric {pname!r} is already a coordinate or a parameter")
        domain[str(pname)] = (float(rng[0]), float(rng[1]))
    if "t" in domain and self.parametric:  # keep time last in the network input
        domain["t"] = domain.pop("t")
    self._n_physical = len([k for k in domain if k != "t"]) - len(self.parametric)
    self.spatial_coordinates = tuple(k for k in domain if k != "t")
    self.time_dependent = "t" in domain
    self.is_ode = not self.spatial_coordinates
    if self.is_ode:
        self.spatial_coordinates = (_DUMMY_COORDINATE,)
        domain = {_DUMMY_COORDINATE: (0.0, 1.0), **domain}
    self.coordinates = self.spatial_coordinates + (("t",) if self.time_dependent else ())
    self.parameters = {str(k): float(v) for k, v in (parameters or {}).items()}
    self._architecture = architecture
    self.unknown_functions = nn.ModuleDict()
    for uname, spec in dict(unknown_functions or {}).items():
        uname = str(uname)
        if uname in self.parameters or uname in self.fields or uname in self.coordinates:
            raise ValueError(
                f"unknown function {uname!r} clashes with a parameter, field or coordinate"
            )
        if isinstance(spec, UnknownFunction):
            fn = spec
        else:
            fn = UnknownFunction.from_spec(uname, spec, coordinate_ranges=domain)
        for inp in fn.inputs:
            if inp not in self.coordinates and inp not in self.fields:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"input {inp!r} of unknown function {uname!r} is neither a coordinate "
                    f"{self.coordinates} nor a field {self.fields}"
                )
        self.unknown_functions[uname] = fn
    self._unknown_names = tuple(self.unknown_functions.keys())
    self.inputs: dict[str, TimeSeries] = {}
    for iname, spec in dict(inputs or {}).items():
        iname = str(iname)
        taken = (
            set(self.parameters)
            | set(self.fields)
            | set(self.coordinates)
            | set(self._unknown_names)
        )
        if iname in taken:
            raise ValueError(
                f"input {iname!r} clashes with a parameter, field, coordinate or unknown"
            )
        if not self.time_dependent:
            raise ValueError(f"input {iname!r}: a time series needs a time-dependent problem")
        self.inputs[iname] = TimeSeries.from_spec(iname, spec)
    self._bc_expressions: dict[str, CompiledExpression] = {}
    self._observables: dict[str, CompiledExpression] = {}
    self.sensors: list[Sensor] = [
        s if isinstance(s, Sensor) else Sensor.from_spec(dict(s)) for s in (sensors or [])
    ]
    self._spec = {
        "equations": equations if not callable(equations) else None,
        "domain": {
            k: list(v)
            for k, v in domain.items()
            if k != _DUMMY_COORDINATE and k not in self.parametric
        },
        "fields": list(self.fields),
        "parameters": dict(self.parameters),
        "initial_condition": None if callable(initial_condition) else initial_condition,
        "initial_velocity": None if callable(initial_velocity) else initial_velocity,
        "boundary_conditions": copy.deepcopy(dict(boundary_conditions or {})),
        "exact_solution": None if callable(exact_solution) else exact_solution,
        "name": name,
        "time_order": time_order,
        "architecture": architecture,
        "unknown_functions": {
            k: cast(UnknownFunction, v).to_spec() for k, v in self.unknown_functions.items()
        },
        "field_weights": dict(field_weights or {}),
        "parametric": {k: list(domain[k]) for k in self.parametric},
        "inputs": {k: v.to_spec() for k, v in self.inputs.items()},
        "sensors": [],  # filled by to_dict, so records written after construction are kept
    }
    self.field_scales: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] = {}
    for fname, value in dict(scales or {}).items():
        if fname not in self.fields:
            raise ValueError(f"scales for {fname!r}, which is not a field {self.fields}")
        offset, scale = (
            (0.0, float(value))
            if isinstance(value, (int, float))
            else (float(value[0]), float(value[1]))
        )
        if scale <= 0:
            raise ValueError(f"scale of {fname!r} must be positive")
        self.field_scales[fname] = (offset, scale)
    self._spec["scales"] = {k: list(v) for k, v in self.field_scales.items()}
    unknown_weights = sorted(set(field_weights or {}) - set(self.fields))
    if unknown_weights:
        raise ValueError(
            f"field_weights for {unknown_weights}, which are not fields {self.fields}"
        )
    self._field_weights = [float((field_weights or {}).get(f, 1.0)) for f in self.fields]
    self._per_field_bcs: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] | None = None
    bcs = dict(boundary_conditions or {})
    if bcs and all(k in self.fields for k in bcs):
        self._per_field_bcs = {f: dict(bcs[f] or {}) for f in bcs}
    elif any(k in self.fields for k in bcs):
        raise ValueError(
            "boundary_conditions mixes field names with condition kinds; give either "
            f"{{kind: options}} for every field or {{field: {{kind: options}}}}: {sorted(bcs)}"
        )

    # Residual: compiled expressions or the user's callable.
    self._residual_fn: Callable | None = None
    self._equations: list[CompiledExpression] = []
    if callable(equations):
        self._residual_fn = equations
        self._needed: set[str] = set()
    else:
        texts = [equations] if isinstance(equations, str) else list(equations)
        if len(texts) != len(self.fields):
            raise ValueError(
                f"{len(texts)} equation(s) for {len(self.fields)} field(s) {self.fields}; "
                "give one equation per field"
            )
        symbols = self.fields + self._unknown_names
        self._equations = [
            compile_expression(t, symbols, self.coordinates, self.parameters) for t in texts
        ]
        self._needed = {p for e in self._equations for p in e.parameters}
    self._ic = self._compile_map(initial_condition, "initial_condition", with_time=False)
    self._ic_fn = initial_condition if callable(initial_condition) else None
    self._velocity = self._compile_map(initial_velocity, "initial_velocity", with_time=False)
    self._velocity_fn = initial_velocity if callable(initial_velocity) else None
    self._exact = self._compile_map(exact_solution, "exact_solution", with_time=True)
    self._exact_fn = exact_solution if callable(exact_solution) else None
    for compiled in list((self._ic or {}).values()) + list((self._velocity or {}).values()):
        self._needed |= set(compiled.parameters)
    if self._exact:
        self._needed |= {p for e in self._exact.values() for p in e.parameters}
    missing = sorted(
        self._needed - set(self.parameters) - set(self._unknown_names) - set(self.inputs)
    )
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Parameters {missing} appear in the equations but are not in parameters="
            f"{sorted(self.parameters)}; pass a value for each (or list it in "
            "trainable_parameters with an initial guess)"
        )

    if time_order is None:
        orders = [e.time_order for e in self._equations]
        time_order = max(orders, default=1) if self.time_dependent else 0
    self.time_order = max(int(time_order), 1) if self.time_dependent else 0

    has_ic = initial_condition is not None and self.time_dependent
    config = PDEConfig(
        name=name,
        domain=[domain[c] for c in self.spatial_coordinates],
        time_domain=domain["t"] if self.time_dependent else (0.0, 0.0),
        parameters=dict(self.parameters),
        boundary_conditions=copy.deepcopy(dict(boundary_conditions or {}))
        if self._per_field_bcs is None
        else {},
        initial_condition={"type": "custom"} if has_ic else {},
        exact_solution={"type": "custom"} if exact_solution is not None else {},
        dimension=len(self.spatial_coordinates),
        input_dim=len(self.spatial_coordinates) + 1,
        output_dim=len(self.fields),
        architecture=architecture,
        device=torch.device(device) if device is not None else None,
        training=training,
        trainable_parameters=list(trainable_parameters),
        parameter_initial_guesses=dict(parameter_initial_guesses or {}),
        observation_data=dict(observation_data) if observation_data else None,
    )
    super().__init__(config)
    self.unknown_functions.to(self.device)
    for sensor in self.sensors:
        sensor.bind(self)
        pending = getattr(sensor, "_pending_values", None)
        if pending is not None:
            sensor.set_values(pending)
            del sensor._pending_values
    if self._per_field_bcs is not None:
        self.config.boundary_conditions = copy.deepcopy(bcs)
        self.boundary_conditions = {
            f: self._parse_boundary_conditions(c) for f, c in self._per_field_bcs.items()
        }

@classmethod
def from_dict(cls, spec: Mapping[str, Any], **overrides: Any) -> CustomPDE:
    """Build from a plain dict (the YAML layout of :meth:`to_dict`); ``overrides`` win."""
    spec = {**spec, **overrides}
    equations = spec.pop("equations", None) or spec.pop("equation", None)
    if equations is None:
        raise ValueError("A custom PDE spec needs an 'equations' entry")
    return cls(equations, **spec)

def build_trainer(
    self,
    architecture: str | None = None,
    config_path: str | None = None,
    device: torch.device | str | None = None,
    model: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    normalize: bool = False,
    derivatives: str = "autograd",
    **training: Any,
):
    """A :class:`~pinnrl.training.trainer.PDETrainer` for this problem with packaged defaults.

    ``derivatives="native"`` takes the residual's derivatives from the
    compiled kernel of :mod:`pinnrl.native` instead of autograd, about
    two to three times as fast per step where it applies: a feed-forward
    ``tanh`` network (with or without layer normalization) on the CPU, equations given as
    text with first and pure second derivatives, macOS. Where it does not
    apply the residual falls back to autograd without notice;
    ``pde.native_active(trainer.model)`` says which one runs.

    ``normalize=True`` non-dimensionalizes the network: its inputs are
    mapped from the domain to ``[-1, 1]`` and its outputs are
    ``offset + scale * net`` with the ``scales`` of the problem (1 for a
    field without one). The equations stay in physical units.

    ``architecture`` names an entry of the ``architectures:`` block of
    ``config.yaml`` (``config_path`` for your own file); ``model``
    overrides keys of that entry (``hidden_dims``, ``activation``,
    ``layer_norm``, ``scale``, ...). ``training`` overrides keys of the
    ``training:`` block (``num_epochs``, ``batch_size``,
    ``num_collocation_points``, ``learning_rate``, ``weight_decay``,
    ``mode``, ``loss_weights``, ...).
    """
    from pinnrl.config import DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH, Config, ModelConfig, TrainingConfig
    from pinnrl.neural_networks import PINNModel
    from pinnrl.training.trainer import PDETrainer

    with open(config_path or DEFAULT_CONFIG_PATH) as f:
        defaults = yaml.safe_load(f)
    training_cfg = copy.deepcopy(defaults.get("training", {}))
    for key, value in training.items():
        if key in ("learning_rate", "weight_decay"):
            training_cfg.setdefault("optimizer_config", {})[key] = value
        elif isinstance(value, Mapping) and isinstance(training_cfg.get(key), Mapping):
            training_cfg[key] = {**training_cfg[key], **value}
        else:
            training_cfg[key] = value
    if (self.config.trainable_parameters or self._unknown_names) and "mode" not in training:
        training_cfg["mode"] = "inverse"
    architecture = architecture or self._architecture
    model = dict(model or {})
    if derivatives not in ("autograd", "native"):
        raise ValueError(f"derivatives must be 'autograd' or 'native', not {derivatives!r}")
    self.derivatives = derivatives
    self._normalized = bool(normalize)
    if normalize:
        model.setdefault("input_bounds", self.normalization_bounds())
        model.setdefault(
            "output_offset", [self.field_scales.get(f, (0.0, 1.0))[0] for f in self.fields]
        )
        model.setdefault(
            "output_scale", [self.field_scales.get(f, (0.0, 1.0))[1] for f in self.fields]
        )
    device = torch.device(device) if device is not None else self.device
    input_dim, output_dim = self.config.input_dim, self.config.output_dim
    assert input_dim is not None and output_dim is not None  # set by PDEBase.__init__
    config = Config.__new__(Config)
    config.device = device
    config.training = TrainingConfig.from_dict(training_cfg)
    config.model = ModelConfig.from_architecture(
        architecture,
        {**defaults.get("architectures", {}).get(architecture, {}), **model},
        input_dim=input_dim,
        output_dim=output_dim,
    )
    config.rl = None
    self.config.training = config.training
    self.device = device
    self.config.device = device
    self.unknown_functions.to(device)
    network = PINNModel(config=config, device=device).to(device)
    network.native_values = derivatives == "native"
    return PDETrainer(model=network, pde=self, config=config, device=device)

def native_active(self, model: torch.nn.Module) -> bool:
    """Whether the residual of ``model`` is computed by the compiled kernel on this machine."""

docs.text:
compute_residual(model, x, t)

Residuals of every equation at x, t, shape (N, k).

With self.derivatives == "native" (build_trainer(derivatives="native")) the derivatives come from the compiled kernel of :mod:pinnrl.native when the network and the equations allow it, and from autograd otherwise.

Source code in pinnrl/pdes/custom.py 
def compute_residual(
    self, model: torch.nn.Module, x: torch.Tensor, t: torch.Tensor
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Residuals of every equation at ``x, t``, shape ``(N, k)``.

    With ``self.derivatives == "native"`` (``build_trainer(derivatives="native")``)
    the derivatives come from the compiled kernel of :mod:`pinnrl.native`
    when the network and the equations allow it, and from autograd otherwise.
    """
    f = Fields(
        model,
        x,
        t,
        self.fields,
        self.coordinates,
        self.device,
        cast("Mapping[str, UnknownFunction]", self.unknown_functions),
        jets=self._native_request(),
    )
    params = self._parameter_values()
    if self.inputs:
        params.update(self._input_values(f.coordinate("t")))
    if self._residual_fn is not None:
        out = self._residual_fn(f, params)
        if not isinstance(out, torch.Tensor):
            out = torch.cat([o.reshape(f.n_points, -1) for o in out], dim=1)
        return out.reshape(f.n_points, -1)
    like = f.value(self.fields[0])
    columns = []
    for expr in self._equations:
        values: dict[str, Any] = dict(params)
        for field in expr.fields:
            values[field] = f.value(field)
        for field, coords in expr.derivatives:
            values[derivative_name(field, coords)] = f.d(field, *coords)
        for c in expr.coordinates:
            values[c] = f.coordinate(c)
        columns.append(expr(values, like))
    return torch.cat(columns, dim=1)

As :meth:PDEBase.compute_loss, with the residual columns weighted by field_weights.

Source code in pinnrl/pdes/custom.py 
def compute_loss(
    self, model: torch.nn.Module, x: torch.Tensor, t: torch.Tensor
) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
    """As :meth:`PDEBase.compute_loss`, with the residual columns weighted by ``field_weights``."""
    losses = super().compute_loss(model, x, t)
    if any(m != 1.0 for m in self._multipliers("residual")):
        losses["residual"] = self._apply_loss_fn(
            self._weighted(self.compute_residual(model, x, t), "residual")
        )
        weights = self._training_option("loss_weights") or {}
        adaptive = self._training_option("adaptive_weights")
        if adaptive is not None and getattr(adaptive, "enabled", False):
            physics = (1.0, 1.0, 1.0)
        else:
            physics = (
                float(weights.get("pde", weights.get("residual", 1.0))),
                float(weights.get("boundary", 10.0)),
                float(weights.get("initial", 10.0)),
            )
        losses["total"] = self.weighted_total(losses, *physics)
    return losses

evaluate_expression(text, model, x, t, parameters=None)

An expression of the fields ("-alpha*u_x") evaluated with model at x, t.

The same language as the equations: fields and their derivatives (by autograd), coordinates, parameters, unknown functions and inputs. Used by sensors and handy for fluxes and other derived quantities. parameters overrides parameter values (tensors allowed), which the sensitivity analysis uses to differentiate through the expression.

Source code in pinnrl/pdes/custom.py 
def evaluate_expression(
    self,
    text: str,
    model: torch.nn.Module,
    x: torch.Tensor,
    t: torch.Tensor | None,
    parameters: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """An expression of the fields (``"-alpha*u_x"``) evaluated with ``model`` at ``x, t``.

    The same language as the equations: fields and their derivatives (by
    autograd), coordinates, parameters, unknown functions and inputs. Used
    by sensors and handy for fluxes and other derived quantities.
    ``parameters`` overrides parameter values (tensors allowed), which the
    sensitivity analysis uses to differentiate through the expression.
    """
    if text not in self._observables:
        expr = compile_expression(
            text, self.fields + self._unknown_names, self.coordinates, self.parameters
        )
        unknown = set(expr.parameters) - set(self.parameters) - set(self.inputs)
        if unknown:
            raise ValueError(f"expression {text!r} uses unknown names {sorted(unknown)}")
        self._observables[text] = expr
    expr = self._observables[text]
    if t is None:
        t = torch.zeros(x.shape[0], 1, device=self.device, dtype=x.dtype)
    f = Fields(
        model,
        x,
        t,
        self.fields,
        self.coordinates,
        self.device,
        cast("Mapping[str, UnknownFunction]", self.unknown_functions),
    )
    values: dict[str, Any] = self._parameter_values()
    values.update(parameters or {})
    if self.inputs:
        values.update(self._input_values(f.coordinate("t")))
    for field in expr.fields:
        values[field] = f.value(field)
    for field, coords in expr.derivatives:
        values[derivative_name(field, coords)] = f.d(field, *coords)
    for c in expr.coordinates:
        values[c] = f.coordinate(c)
    return expr(values, f.value(self.fields[0]))

observe(noise=None, seed=0)

Fill every sensor's records from the exact solution, through its operator, with noise.

noise overrides each sensor's own standard deviation; the seed is offset per sensor so records are independent. Needs an exact solution.

Source code in pinnrl/pdes/custom.py 
def observe(self, noise: float | None = None, seed: int | None = 0) -> list[Sensor]:
    """Fill every sensor's records from the exact solution, through its operator, with noise.

    ``noise`` overrides each sensor's own standard deviation; the seed is
    offset per sensor so records are independent. Needs an exact solution.
    """
    if not self.has_exact_solution:
        raise ValueError(f"{self.config.name}: observe() needs a configured exact_solution")
    pde = self

    class _Exact(torch.nn.Module):
        def forward(self, inp):
            d = len(pde.spatial_coordinates)
            return pde.exact_solution(inp[:, :d], inp[:, d:])

    exact = _Exact()
    # Read the TRUE parameters, not the current guesses (as generate_synthetic_observations).
    saved = self._trainable_params
    try:
        if self._true_parameters:
            self._trainable_params = nn.ParameterDict()
        for k, sensor in enumerate(self.sensors):
            sensor.observe(
                exact, noise=noise, seed=None if seed is None else int(seed) + 1000 * k
            )
    finally:
        self._trainable_params = saved
    return self.sensors

docs.title: surrogate_misfit
docs.text:
surrogate_misfit(model, x, t, y, thetas, field=0)

Sum of squared residuals of the parametric surrogate against data, per parameter value.

x (N, d) holds the physical coordinates of the observations, t (N, 1) their times and y (N, 1) their values; thetas is (M, p) over the parametric axes in their declared order. Returns (M,), the vectorized misfit a swarm consumes.

Source code in pinnrl/pdes/custom.py 
def surrogate_misfit(
    self,
    model: torch.nn.Module,
    x: torch.Tensor,
    t: torch.Tensor,
    y: torch.Tensor,
    thetas: Any,
    field: int = 0,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Sum of squared residuals of the parametric surrogate against data, per parameter value.

    ``x`` ``(N, d)`` holds the physical coordinates of the observations,
    ``t`` ``(N, 1)`` their times and ``y`` ``(N, 1)`` their values;
    ``thetas`` is ``(M, p)`` over the parametric axes in their declared
    order. Returns ``(M,)``, the vectorized misfit a swarm consumes.
    """
    if not self.parametric:
        raise ValueError("surrogate_misfit needs a problem with parametric axes")
    thetas_t = torch.as_tensor(
        np.asarray(thetas, dtype=np.float64), dtype=x.dtype, device=self.device
    )
    thetas_t = thetas_t.reshape(-1, len(self.parametric))
    m, n = thetas_t.shape[0], x.shape[0]
    xx = x.to(self.device).reshape(n, -1).repeat(m, 1)
    tt = t.to(self.device).reshape(n, 1).repeat(m, 1)
    th = thetas_t.repeat_interleave(n, dim=0)
    with torch.no_grad():
        pred = model(torch.cat([xx, th, tt], dim=1))[:, field : field + 1]
    err = (pred - y.to(self.device).reshape(n, 1).repeat(m, 1)) ** 2
    return err.reshape(m, n).sum(dim=1)

def normalization_bounds(self) -> list[list[float]]:
    """One ``[lo, hi]`` per network input (the spatial axes, then time), from the domain."""

docs.text:
evaluate_unknown(name, x, t=None, model=None, truth=False)

The learned (or, with truth=True, the true) unknown function name at x, t.

x is (N, d) over the spatial coordinates and t (N, 1); model is needed when the function depends on a field.

Source code in pinnrl/pdes/custom.py 
def evaluate_unknown(
    self,
    name: str,
    x: torch.Tensor,
    t: torch.Tensor | None = None,
    model: torch.nn.Module | None = None,
    truth: bool = False,
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """The learned (or, with ``truth=True``, the true) unknown function ``name`` at ``x, t``.

    ``x`` is ``(N, d)`` over the spatial coordinates and ``t`` ``(N, 1)``;
    ``model`` is needed when the function depends on a field.
    """
    fn = cast(UnknownFunction, self.unknown_functions[name])
    x = x.to(self.device).reshape(x.shape[0], -1)
    values: dict[str, torch.Tensor] = {}
    for i, c in enumerate(self.spatial_coordinates):
        values[c] = x[:, i : i + 1]
    if t is not None:
        values["t"] = t.to(self.device).reshape(-1, 1)
    if any(i in self.fields for i in fn.inputs):
        if model is None:
            raise ValueError(f"{name!r} depends on a field; pass the model")
        tt = values.get("t", torch.zeros(x.shape[0], 1, device=self.device))
        u = model(torch.cat([x, tt], dim=1))
        for j, field in enumerate(self.fields):
            values[field] = u[:, j : j + 1]
    inputs = {i: values[i] for i in fn.inputs}
    return fn.truth(inputs) if truth else fn(inputs)

docs.text:
unknown_function_error(name, num_points=2000, model=None)

Relative L2 error of the learned unknown name against its truth.

Over a tensor grid of its inputs when they are all coordinates (:meth:UnknownFunction.grid), else over num_points uniform space-time points with the fields taken from model.

Source code in pinnrl/pdes/custom.py 
@torch.no_grad()
def unknown_function_error(
    self, name: str, num_points: int = 2000, model: torch.nn.Module | None = None
) -> float:
    """Relative L2 error of the learned unknown ``name`` against its truth.

    Over a tensor grid of its inputs when they are all coordinates
    (:meth:`UnknownFunction.grid`), else over ``num_points`` uniform
    space-time points with the fields taken from ``model``.
    """
    fn = cast(UnknownFunction, self.unknown_functions[name])
    if all(i in self.coordinates for i in fn.inputs):
        n = max(2, int(round(num_points ** (1.0 / len(fn.inputs)))))
        return fn.relative_error(n=n)
    x, t = self._sample_uniform(num_points)
    pred = self.evaluate_unknown(name, x, t, model=model)
    true = self.evaluate_unknown(name, x, t, model=model, truth=True)
    return float(torch.linalg.norm(pred - true) / torch.linalg.norm(true))

    x,

    fields,

The network outputs and their derivatives at one batch of points, computed on demand.

f.u is the field u (shape (N, 1)), f.u_xx its second x-derivative, f.x and f.t the coordinates; f.d("u", "x", "t") is the same as f.u_xt. Each derivative is computed by autograd once and cached, so a residual can use f.u_x and f.u_xx without paying for the first derivative twice.

Evaluate model at x, t (fresh leaf copies that require grad).

jets = (first, second) names the coordinates whose first and pure second derivatives the residual needs; when the model can supply them by its compiled kernel (model.jets, :mod:pinnrl.native) they are taken from there and nothing is differentiated by autograd.

Source code in pinnrl/pdes/custom.py 
def __init__(
    self,
    model: torch.nn.Module,
    x: torch.Tensor,
    t: torch.Tensor,
    fields: Sequence[str],
    coordinates: Sequence[str],
    device: torch.device,
    unknowns: Mapping[str, UnknownFunction] | None = None,
    jets: tuple[Sequence[str], Sequence[str]] | None = None,
):
    """Evaluate ``model`` at ``x, t`` (fresh leaf copies that require grad).

    ``jets = (first, second)`` names the coordinates whose first and pure
    second derivatives the residual needs; when the model can supply them
    by its compiled kernel (``model.jets``, :mod:`pinnrl.native`) they are
    taken from there and nothing is differentiated by autograd.
    """
    self._x = x.detach().to(device).requires_grad_(True)
    self._t = t.detach().to(device).requires_grad_(True)
    self._fields = tuple(fields)
    self._coordinates = tuple(coordinates)
    self._unknowns: dict[str, UnknownFunction] = dict(unknowns or {})
    self._cache: dict[tuple[str, tuple[str, ...]], torch.Tensor] = {}
    self._spatial = [c for c in self._coordinates if c != "t"]
    self.native = False
    inp = torch.cat([self._x, self._t], dim=1)
    model_jets: Callable | None = getattr(model, "jets", None)
    if jets is not None and model_jets is not None:
        columns = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(self._spatial)}
        columns["t"] = self._x.shape[1]  # an ODE keeps a dummy spatial column
        got = model_jets(
            inp.detach(), [columns[c] for c in jets[0]], [columns[c] for c in jets[1]]
        )
        if got is not None:
            self._u, du, d2u = got
            names = {i: c for c, i in columns.items()}
            for j, field in enumerate(self._fields):
                for col, g in du.items():
                    self._cache[(field, (names[col],))] = g[:, j : j + 1]
                for col, g in d2u.items():
                    self._cache[(field, (names[col], names[col]))] = g[:, j : j + 1]
            self.native = True
            return
    self._u = model(inp)

def value(self, field: str) -> torch.Tensor:
    """The field ``field`` as predicted by the network, or an unknown function, shape ``(N, 1)``."""
    if field in self._unknowns:
        key = (field, ())
        if key not in self._cache:
            fn = self._unknowns[field]
            self._cache[key] = fn(
                {
                    name: self.coordinate(name)
                    if name in self._coordinates
                    else self.value(name)
                    for name in fn.inputs
                }
            )
        return self._cache[key]
    j = self._fields.index(field)
    return self._u[:, j : j + 1]

d(field, *coordinates)

∂^n field / ∂coordinates, e.g. f.d("u", "x", "x") for u_xx.

Source code in pinnrl/pdes/custom.py 
def d(self, field: str, *coordinates: str) -> torch.Tensor:
    """``∂^n field / ∂coordinates``, e.g. ``f.d("u", "x", "x")`` for ``u_xx``."""
    key = (field, tuple(sorted(coordinates)))
    if not coordinates:
        return self.value(field)
    if key not in self._cache:
        if self.native and field in self._fields:
            raise RuntimeError(
                f"the derivative {field}_{''.join(key[1])} was not requested from the native kernel"
            )
        previous = self.d(field, *key[1][:-1])
        wrt = self._t if key[1][-1] == "t" else self._x
        grad = PDEBase._grad(previous, wrt)
        if key[1][-1] != "t":
            i = self._spatial.index(key[1][-1])
            grad = grad[:, i : i + 1]
        self._cache[key] = grad
    return self._cache[key]

def __getattr__(self, name: str) -> torch.Tensor:
    """``f.u``, ``f.u_xx``, ``f.x`` by attribute; anything else is an error."""
    if name.startswith("_"):
        raise AttributeError(name)
    if name in self._fields or name in self._unknowns:
        return self.value(name)
    if name in self._coordinates:
        return self.coordinate(name)
    split = split_derivative(name, self._fields + tuple(self._unknowns), self._coordinates)
    if split is not None:
        return self.d(split[0], *split[1])
    raise AttributeError(
        f"{name!r} is not a field {self._fields}, an unknown function {tuple(self._unknowns)}, "
        f"a coordinate {self._coordinates} or a derivative such as 'u_xx'"
    )

A learnable function of coordinates and fields that replaces a coefficient.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default name str

The symbol it takes in the equations ("alpha").

required inputs Sequence[str]

Names it depends on, coordinates ("x", "t") or fields ("u"), in the order they enter the network.

None hidden Sequence[int]

Hidden widths, default (32, 32).

(32, 32) activation str

tanh (default), sigmoid, relu, softplus, gelu or silu; a monotone network needs a non-decreasing one.

'tanh' positive bool

Output through a softplus, so the function is positive.

False bounds Sequence[float] | None

(lo, hi): output through a sigmoid into that interval.

None monotone Mapping[str, str] | str | None

{input: "increasing" | "decreasing"} (or one of those strings when there is a single input): the function is monotone in those inputs, by non-negative weights on every path from them.

None initial float

The constant the function starts at (the network's last layer starts at zero), the analogue of a scalar's initial guess. An anchored function starts at its anchor value everywhere.

1.0 anchor Mapping[str, Any] | None

{"at": {input: coordinate}, "value": v} ("at" may be a number when there is a single input): the function takes v at that point exactly, whatever the weights, by subtracting its own value there. Combined with monotone this fixes the sign everywhere: a closure with anchor={"at": X_eq, "value": 0} and monotone="increasing" is non-negative above X_eq. v must be inside bounds or positive with positive; with a basis the constant mode is dropped, since the anchor supplies it.

None basis Mapping[str, Any] | None

{"type": "cosine" | "legendre", "modes": n}: instead of a network, a linear combination of n fixed modes of a single input, so the unknown is the coefficient vector :attr:coefficients and the identifiability of each mode can be analysed like a parameter (K48). hidden, activation and monotone do not apply; positive and bounds still do.

None truth str | Callable | None

The true function as an expression in the inputs ("0.1 + 0.05*t", with pi, exp, heaviside, ...) or a callable truth(**inputs) -> (N, 1). Used for synthetic data, for exact solutions that mention the unknown, and by :meth:relative_error.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

For an empty input list, an unknown activation, a non-monotone activation with monotone, inconsistent bounds, an initial or anchor value outside the admissible set, or an anchor that does not give every input.

def __init__(
    self,
    name: str,
    inputs: Sequence[str],
    *,
    input_ranges: Mapping[str, Sequence[float]] | None = None,
    hidden: Sequence[int] = (32, 32),
    activation: str = "tanh",
    positive: bool = False,
    bounds: Sequence[float] | None = None,
    monotone: Mapping[str, str] | str | None = None,
    initial: float = 1.0,
    truth: str | Callable | None = None,
    basis: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
    anchor: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
):
    super().__init__()
    self.name = str(name)
    self.inputs = tuple(str(i) for i in inputs)
    if not self.inputs:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown function {name!r} needs at least one input")
    if activation not in _ACTIVATIONS:
        raise ValueError(
            f"unknown activation {activation!r} for {name!r}; one of {sorted(_ACTIVATIONS)}"
        )
    if isinstance(monotone, str):
        if len(self.inputs) != 1:
            raise ValueError(
                f"monotone={monotone!r} for {name!r} needs a single input; "
                "give {input: direction} instead"
            )
        monotone = {self.inputs[0]: monotone}
    self.monotone: dict[str, str] = {}
    for key, direction in dict(monotone or {}).items():
        if key not in self.inputs:
            raise ValueError(
                f"monotone input {key!r} is not an input of {name!r} {self.inputs}"
            )
        if direction not in ("increasing", "decreasing"):
            raise ValueError(f"monotone direction for {key!r} must be increasing or decreasing")
        self.monotone[key] = direction
    if self.monotone and activation not in _MONOTONE_ACTIVATIONS:
        raise ValueError(
            f"a monotone network needs a non-decreasing activation, not {activation!r}"
        )
    if bounds is not None:
        bounds = (float(bounds[0]), float(bounds[1]))
        if not bounds[0] < bounds[1]:
            raise ValueError(f"bounds for {name!r} must satisfy lo < hi, got {bounds}")
    self.positive = bool(positive) and bounds is None
    self.bounds = bounds
    self.hidden = tuple(int(h) for h in hidden)
    self.activation = activation
    self.initial = float(initial)
    ranges = {k: (float(v[0]), float(v[1])) for k, v in (input_ranges or {}).items()}
    self.input_ranges: dict[str, tuple[float, float]] = {
        i: ranges.get(i, (-1.0, 1.0)) for i in self.inputs
    }
    lo = torch.tensor([self.input_ranges[i][0] for i in self.inputs])
    hi = torch.tensor([self.input_ranges[i][1] for i in self.inputs])
    self.register_buffer("_lo", lo)
    self.register_buffer("_hi", hi)

    self.anchor: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    if anchor is not None:
        at = anchor.get("at") if isinstance(anchor, Mapping) else None
        if at is None or "value" not in anchor:
            raise ValueError(f"anchor of {name!r} needs 'at' and 'value'")
        if not isinstance(at, Mapping):
            if len(self.inputs) != 1:
                raise ValueError(f"anchor 'at' of {name!r} must give every input {self.inputs}")
            at = {self.inputs[0]: at}
        missing = [i for i in self.inputs if i not in at]
        if missing:
            raise ValueError(f"anchor of {name!r} gives no coordinate for {missing}")
        self.anchor = {
            "at": {i: float(at[i]) for i in self.inputs},
            "value": float(anchor["value"]),
        }
        self.initial = self.anchor["value"]
        z_a = torch.tensor([[self.anchor["at"][i] for i in self.inputs]])
        self.register_buffer("_z_anchor", 2.0 * (z_a - lo) / (hi - lo) - 1.0)

    self.basis: dict[str, Any] | None = None
    if basis is not None:
        if len(self.inputs) != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"a basis needs a single input; {name!r} has {self.inputs}")
        if self.monotone:
            raise ValueError("monotone is not available with a basis")
        self.basis = {
            "type": str(basis.get("type", "cosine")),
            "modes": int(basis.get("modes", 6)),
        }
        self.net = nn.Sequential(
            _BasisFeatures(
                self.basis["type"], self.basis["modes"], skip_constant=self.anchor is not None
            ),
            _ConstrainedLinear(self.basis["modes"], 1),
        )
    else:
        signs = [
            {"increasing": 1, "decreasing": -1}.get(self.monotone.get(i, ""), 0)
            for i in self.inputs
        ]
        layers: list[nn.Module] = []
        widths = [len(self.inputs), *self.hidden, 1]
        for k, (n_in, n_out) in enumerate(zip(widths[:-1], widths[1:], strict=True)):
            if k == 0:
                layers.append(_ConstrainedLinear(n_in, n_out, signs=signs))
            else:
                layers.append(_ConstrainedLinear(n_in, n_out, all_positive=bool(self.monotone)))
            if k < len(widths) - 2:
                layers.append(_ACTIVATIONS[activation]())
        self.net = nn.Sequential(*layers)
    self._start_at_constant(self.initial)

    self._truth_fn: Callable | None = truth if callable(truth) else None
    self._truth_expr = None
    self.truth_text: str | None = None
    if truth is not None and not callable(truth):
        self.truth_text = str(truth)
        self._truth_expr = compile_expression(self.truth_text, (), self.inputs)
        if self._truth_expr.parameters:
            raise ValueError(
                f"truth {self.truth_text!r} of {name!r} uses {self._truth_expr.parameters}, "
                f"which are not among its inputs {self.inputs}"
            )

def modes(self, values: Mapping[str, torch.Tensor]) -> torch.Tensor:
    """The basis modes at ``values``, ``(N, modes)``, for sensitivity analyses."""
    if self.basis is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{self.name!r} is a network; modes need basis=...")
    z = self._stack(values)
    z = 2.0 * (z - self._lo) / (self._hi - self._lo) - 1.0
    return self.net[0](z)

    """The dict that rebuilds this function (weights excluded; a callable truth is left out)."""
    spec: dict[str, Any] = {
        "inputs": list(self.inputs),

    if self.bounds is not None:
        spec["bounds"] = list(self.bounds)

def forward(self, values: Mapping[str, torch.Tensor]) -> torch.Tensor:
    """The learned function at ``values`` (``{input: (N, 1)}``), shape ``(N, 1)``."""
    z = self._stack(values)
    z = 2.0 * (z - self._lo) / (self._hi - self._lo) - 1.0
    out = self._raw(z)
    if self.bounds is not None:
        lo, hi = self.bounds
        return lo + (hi - lo) * torch.sigmoid(out)
    if self.positive:
        return nn.functional.softplus(out)
    return out

def truth(self, values: Mapping[str, torch.Tensor]) -> torch.Tensor:
    """The true function at ``values``, shape ``(N, 1)``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When no truth was given.
    """
    if self._truth_fn is not None:
        out = self._truth_fn(**{i: values[i].reshape(-1, 1) for i in self.inputs})
        return out.reshape(-1, 1)
    if self._truth_expr is None:
        raise ValueError(f"unknown function {self.name!r} has no truth to compare with")
    like = values[self.inputs[0]].reshape(-1, 1)
    return self._truth_expr({i: values[i].reshape(-1, 1) for i in self.inputs}, like)

def fit(
    self,
    values: Mapping[str, Any],
    targets: Any,
    steps: int = 3000,
    lr: float = 1e-2,
) -> float:
    """Pre-train the function to ``targets`` at the input ``values`` (least squares, Adam).

    The start of an inverse run when a pointwise estimate of the function
    exists, e.g. a closure read off a dense record (J07b). Returns the
    final mean-squared error.
    """
    inputs = {
        i: torch.as_tensor(np.asarray(values[i]), dtype=torch.float32).reshape(-1, 1)
        for i in self.inputs
    }
    y = torch.as_tensor(np.asarray(targets), dtype=torch.float32).reshape(-1, 1)
    optimizer = torch.optim.Adam(self.parameters(), lr=lr)
    loss = torch.zeros(())
    for _ in range(int(steps)):
        optimizer.zero_grad()
        loss = ((self(inputs) - y) ** 2).mean()
        loss.backward()
        optimizer.step()
    return float(loss.detach())

def grid(
    self, n: int = 256, device: torch.device | str | None = None
) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
    """``n`` points per input on a tensor grid over the input ranges (``n**len(inputs)`` in all)."""
    axes = [
        torch.linspace(*self.input_ranges[i], n, device=device, dtype=self._lo.dtype)
        for i in self.inputs
    ]
    mesh = torch.meshgrid(*axes, indexing="ij")
    return {i: m.reshape(-1, 1) for i, m in zip(self.inputs, mesh, strict=True)}

@torch.no_grad()
def relative_error(
    self, values: Mapping[str, torch.Tensor] | None = None, n: int = 256
) -> float:
    """``||f - f*|| / ||f*||`` against the truth, on ``values`` or on :meth:`grid`."""
    if values is None:
        values = self.grid(n, device=self._lo.device)
    truth = self.truth(values)
    return float(torch.linalg.norm(self(values) - truth) / torch.linalg.norm(truth))

def __init__(
    self,
    t: Sequence[float] | np.ndarray,
    values: Sequence[float] | np.ndarray,
    *,
    name: str = "input",
    path: str | None = None,
    time_column: str | None = None,
    value_column: str | None = None,
):
    t_arr = np.asarray(t, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1)
    v_arr = np.asarray(values, dtype=np.float64).reshape(-1)
    if t_arr.shape != v_arr.shape:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: {t_arr.size} times but {v_arr.size} values")
    if t_arr.size < 2:
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: a time series needs at least two samples")
    if not np.all(np.diff(t_arr) > 0):
        raise ValueError(f"{name}: sample times must be strictly increasing")
    self.name = name
    self.t = t_arr
    self.values = v_arr
    self.path = path
    self.time_column = time_column
    self.value_column = value_column
    self._t_torch = torch.as_tensor(self.t)
    self._v_torch = torch.as_tensor(self.values)

@classmethod
def from_file(
    cls,
    path: str | Path,
    time_column: str = "t",
    value_column: str | None = None,
    name: str | None = None,
) -> TimeSeries:
    """Read a ``.csv`` (header row) or ``.npz`` file.

    ``value_column`` defaults to the first column that is not the time
    column. Rows that do not parse as numbers are skipped.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If a column is missing or the extension is not supported.
    """
    path = Path(path)
    if path.suffix.lower() == ".npz":
        data = np.load(path)
        columns = {k: np.asarray(data[k]).reshape(-1) for k in data.files}
    elif path.suffix.lower() in (".csv", ".txt"):
        with open(path, newline="") as f:
            reader = csv.DictReader(f)
            rows = [r for r in reader]
        if not rows:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}: empty file")
        columns = {}
        for key in rows[0]:
            vals = []
            for r in rows:
                try:
                    vals.append(float(r[key]))
                except (TypeError, ValueError):
                    vals.append(np.nan)
            columns[key.strip()] = np.asarray(vals)
    else:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: use a .csv or .npz file")
    if time_column not in columns:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: no column {time_column!r}; columns are {sorted(columns)}")
    if value_column is None:
        others = [k for k in columns if k != time_column]
        if not others:
            raise ValueError(f"{path}: no value column besides {time_column!r}")
        value_column = others[0]
    if value_column not in columns:
        raise ValueError(f"{path}: no column {value_column!r}; columns are {sorted(columns)}")
    t, v = columns[time_column], columns[value_column]
    keep = ~(np.isnan(t) | np.isnan(v))
    order = np.argsort(t[keep], kind="stable")
    return cls(
        t[keep][order],
        v[keep][order],
        name=name or value_column,
        path=str(path),
        time_column=time_column,
        value_column=value_column,
    )

@classmethod
def from_spec(cls, name: str, spec: Any, base_dir: str | Path | None = None) -> TimeSeries:
    """Build from a :class:`TimeSeries`, a file spec or inline samples.

    ``spec`` is a :class:`TimeSeries`, ``{"path", "time_column", "value_column"}``
    or ``{"t": [...], "values": [...]}``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: For a spec of another shape.
    """
    if isinstance(spec, TimeSeries):
        return spec
    if isinstance(spec, Mapping):
        if "path" in spec:
            path = Path(spec["path"])
            if base_dir is not None and not path.is_absolute():
                path = Path(base_dir) / path
            return cls.from_file(
                path,
                time_column=spec.get("time_column", "t"),
                value_column=spec.get("value_column"),
                name=name,
            )
        if "t" in spec and "values" in spec:
            return cls(spec["t"], spec["values"], name=name)
    raise ValueError(
        f"input {name!r}: give a TimeSeries, {{'path': ..., 'time_column': ..., "
        f"'value_column': ...}} or {{'t': [...], 'values': [...]}}"
    )

Source code in pinnrl/pdes/inputs.py 
def __call__(self, t: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """The signal at ``t`` (any shape), with ``t``'s dtype and device; no gradient flows."""
    tt = self._t_torch.to(device=t.device, dtype=torch.float64)
    vv = self._v_torch.to(device=t.device, dtype=torch.float64)
    q = t.detach().to(torch.float64).reshape(-1)
    idx = torch.searchsorted(tt, q, right=True).clamp(1, tt.numel() - 1)
    t0, t1 = tt[idx - 1], tt[idx]
    v0, v1 = vv[idx - 1], vv[idx]
    w = ((q - t0) / (t1 - t0)).clamp(0.0, 1.0)
    out = v0 + w * (v1 - v0)
    return out.reshape(t.shape).to(dtype=t.dtype)

def observe(
    self, model: torch.nn.Module, noise: float | None = None, seed: int | None = 0
) -> Sensor:
    """Fill the records from ``model`` (the exact solution wrapped, or a trained network)."""
    clean = self.predict(model).detach()  # autograd stays on: the expression may need u_x
    sigma = self.noise if noise is None else float(noise)
    if sigma > 0:
        gen = torch.Generator(device="cpu")
        if seed is not None:
            gen.manual_seed(int(seed))
        clean = clean + sigma * torch.randn(clean.shape, generator=gen).to(clean.device)
    return self.set_values(clean)

The sensor's weighted data misfit weight * reduce((H[u] - y) / scale).

With time_cutoff only the records stamped at or before it count (time-marching, :meth:PDETrainer.train_windows).

Source code in pinnrl/pdes/sensors.py 
def loss(
    self, model: torch.nn.Module, reduce, time_cutoff: float | None = None
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """The sensor's weighted data misfit ``weight * reduce((H[u] - y) / scale)``.

    With ``time_cutoff`` only the records stamped at or before it count
    (time-marching, :meth:`PDETrainer.train_windows`).
    """
    if self.values is None:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{self.name} has no records; call pde.observe() or sensor.set_values()"
        )
    error = (self.predict(model) - self.values.to(self._pde.device)) / self.loss_scale()
    if time_cutoff is not None:
        keep = torch.as_tensor(self.times <= float(time_cutoff), device=error.device)
        if not bool(keep.any()):
            return torch.zeros((), device=error.device)
        error = error[keep.reshape(-1)]
    return self.weight * reduce(error)

def misfit(self, model: torch.nn.Module) -> float:
    """The chi-square of the records under ``model``: ``sum(((H[u] - y) / noise)^2)``.

    The sensor's own judgement of a fit, in units of its noise: about
    ``n_records`` when the model reproduces the records to their noise.

    Raises:
        ValueError: Without records or with ``noise == 0``.
    """
    if self.values is None:
        raise ValueError(f"{self.name} has no records; call pde.observe() or set_values()")
    if self.noise <= 0:
        raise ValueError(f"{self.name}: misfit needs noise > 0")
    with torch.enable_grad():  # the expression may need derivatives of the fields
        pred = self.predict(model).detach()
    error = (pred - self.values.to(pred.device)).reshape(-1) / self.noise
    return float((error**2).sum())

def points(self) -> tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor]:
    """Points on the face for every record, and the evaluation times."""
    domain = self._pde.domain
    t = self.evaluation_times()
    centre = [0.5 * (lo + hi) for lo, hi in domain]
    x = list(self.position) if self.position is not None else centre

    xx = torch.tensor(x, dtype=t.dtype).reshape(1, -1).expand(t.shape[0], -1)

The weighted integral of the expression at every record time, (M, 1).

Source code in pinnrl/pdes/sensors.py 
def predict(
    self, model: torch.nn.Module, parameters: dict[str, Any] | None = None
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """The weighted integral of the expression at every record time, ``(M, 1)``."""
    nodes, volume = self._grid()
    x, t = self.points()
    values = self._pde.evaluate_expression(self.expression, model, x, t, parameters)
    if self.weight_expression is not None:
        if self._weight_compiled is None:
            self._weight_compiled = compile_expression(
                self.weight_expression, (), self._pde.spatial_coordinates, self._pde.parameters
            )
        inputs: dict[str, Any] = dict(self._pde.parameters)
        for i, c in enumerate(self._pde.spatial_coordinates):
            inputs[c] = x[:, i : i + 1].to(values.device)
        values = values * self._weight_compiled(inputs, values)
    total = values.reshape(-1, nodes.shape[0]).sum(dim=1, keepdim=True) * volume
    if self.normalize:
        total = total / (volume * nodes.shape[0])
    return total

def sensor_jacobian(
    pde: Any, parameters: Sequence[str], sensors: Sequence[Sensor] | None = None
) -> torch.Tensor:
    """``d H[u*] / d theta`` of the closed-form solution for every record, ``(M_total, p)``.

    The exact solution is evaluated with per-record copies of the parameters
    that require grad, the sensor expressions (with their derivatives) are
    applied to it, and autograd gives the sensitivity of each record. Feed the
    result to :func:`pinnrl.analysis.fisher_information` with each sensor's
    noise to get the Fisher information and Cramér–Rao bound of a layout.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the PDE has no expression-valued exact solution or a
            name is not one of its parameters.
    """
    compiled = getattr(pde, "_exact", None)
    if not compiled:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{pde.config.name}: sensor_jacobian needs an expression-valued exact_solution"
        )
    unknown = [p for p in parameters if p not in pde.parameters]
    if unknown:
        raise ValueError(
            f"{unknown} are not parameters of {pde.config.name}: {list(pde.parameters)}"
        )
    sensors = list(pde.sensors if sensors is None else sensors)
    rows = []
    for sensor in sensors:
        sensor.bind(pde)
        x, t = sensor.points()
        n = x.shape[0]
        thetas = {
            name: torch.full(
                (n, 1), float(pde.parameters[name]), dtype=torch.float64, requires_grad=True
            )
            for name in parameters
        }

        pred = sensor.predict(
            _ExactWithThetas(pde, compiled, x.shape[1], thetas), parameters=thetas
        )
        records = sensor.n_records
        cols = []
        for name in parameters:
            g = torch.autograd.grad(pred.sum(), thetas[name], retain_graph=True, allow_unused=True)[
                0
            ]
            g = torch.zeros(n, 1, dtype=torch.float64) if g is None else g
            # an integral sensor has one theta copy per quadrature node: sum them per record
            cols.append(g.reshape(records, -1).sum(dim=1))
        rows.append(torch.stack(cols, dim=1))
    return torch.cat(rows, dim=0)

def sensor_misfit(
    sensors: Sequence[Sensor], model: torch.nn.Module, level: float = 0.999
) -> SensorMisfit:
    """:class:`SensorMisfit` of ``model`` over the sensors that carry records.

    Raises:
        ValueError: When no sensor has records, or a sensor with records has no noise.
    """
    from scipy.stats import chi2 as chi2_dist

    per_sensor = {s.name: s.misfit(model) for s in sensors if s.values is not None}
    if not per_sensor:
        raise ValueError("sensor_misfit needs at least one sensor with records")
    n = sum(s.n_records for s in sensors if s.values is not None)
    level = float(level)
    if not 0.0 < level < 1.0:
        raise ValueError(f"level must be in (0, 1), got {level}")
    return SensorMisfit(
        chi2=float(sum(per_sensor.values())),
        n=int(n),
        limit=float(chi2_dist.ppf(level, n)),
        level=level,
        per_sensor=per_sensor,
    )

SensorMisfit(chi2, n, limit, level, per_sensor=dict())

The chi-square of a model against the sensor records, and whether it passes.

chi2 is the sum over all records of the squared error in units of each sensor's noise; n is the number of records, so reduced is about 1 for a model that explains the records to their noise. limit is the level quantile of the chi-square distribution with n degrees of freedom: a model whose fields fit the data are accepted when chi2 <= limit. In the twins of J06 and J07 a run whose fit fails this test has also missed the unknown, and it is the test the run itself can make, without the truth.

def compile_expression(
    text: str,
    fields: Sequence[str],
    coordinates: Sequence[str],
    known_parameters: Iterable[str] = (),
) -> CompiledExpression:
    """Parse ``text`` and compile it into a torch callable.

    Args:
        text: The expression, e.g. ``"u_t + u*u_x - nu*u_xx"``.
        fields: Field (output) names.
        coordinates: Coordinate (input) names, including ``"t"`` when the
            problem is time dependent.
        known_parameters: Parameter names the caller can supply; any other
            free name is still accepted and reported in ``parameters`` so the
            caller can raise a precise error.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the text does not parse or uses an unknown function.
    """
    fields = tuple(fields)
    coordinates = tuple(coordinates)
    local: dict[str, object] = {}
    seen_fields, seen_derivs, seen_coords, seen_params = [], [], [], []
    for ident in dict.fromkeys(_IDENTIFIER.findall(text)):
        canonical = _FUNCTION_ALIASES.get(ident, ident)
        if ident in fields:
            local[ident] = sympy.Symbol(ident)
            seen_fields.append(ident)
            continue
        split = split_derivative(ident, fields, coordinates)
        if split is not None:
            name = derivative_name(*split)
            local[ident] = sympy.Symbol(name)
            if split not in seen_derivs:
                seen_derivs.append(split)
            continue
        if ident in coordinates:
            local[ident] = sympy.Symbol(ident)
            seen_coords.append(ident)
        elif canonical in _SYMPY_FUNCTIONS:
            local[ident] = _SYMPY_FUNCTIONS[canonical]
        elif canonical in TORCH_FUNCTIONS:
            local[ident] = getattr(sympy, canonical)
        elif ident in _CONSTANTS:
            local[ident] = _CONSTANTS[ident]
        else:
            looks_like = [f for f in fields if ident.startswith(f + "_")]
            if looks_like:
                raise ValueError(
                    f"{ident!r} in {text!r} reads as a derivative of {looks_like[0]!r}, but "
                    f"{ident[len(looks_like[0]) + 1 :]!r} is not made of the coordinates "
                    f"{tuple(coordinates)}"
                )
            local[ident] = sympy.Symbol(ident)
            seen_params.append(ident)
    try:
        expr = parse_expr(text, local_dict=local, transformations=_TRANSFORMATIONS)
    except Exception as exc:  # SyntaxError, TokenError, TypeError from SymPy
        raise ValueError(f"Cannot parse expression {text!r}: {exc}") from exc
    if not isinstance(expr, (sympy.Expr, sympy.Basic)):
        raise ValueError(f"Expression {text!r} is not a formula")
    for func in expr.atoms(sympy.Function):
        name = type(func).__name__
        if name not in TORCH_FUNCTIONS and name not in _SYMPY_FUNCTIONS:
            raise ValueError(
                f"Unknown function {name!r} in {text!r}; available: "
                + ", ".join(sorted(k for k in TORCH_FUNCTIONS if k[0].islower()))
            )
    deriv_names = [derivative_name(f, c) for f, c in seen_derivs]
    args = tuple(seen_fields + deriv_names + seen_coords + seen_params)
    symbols = [sympy.Symbol(a) for a in args]
    fn = sympy.lambdify(symbols, expr, modules=[TORCH_FUNCTIONS, {"pi": math.pi}])
    return CompiledExpression(
        text=text,
        expr=expr,
        fields=tuple(seen_fields),
        derivatives=tuple(seen_derivs),
        coordinates=tuple(seen_coords),
        parameters=tuple(seen_params),
        _fn=fn,
        _args=args,
    )

def __call__(self, values: dict[str, torch.Tensor | float], like: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Evaluate with ``values`` (name to tensor or number); constants broadcast to ``like``.

    Derivative names use the subscript spelling the expression used
    (``"u_xx"``), as :func:`derivative_name` produces.
    """
    out = self._fn(*(values[a] for a in self._args))
    if not isinstance(out, torch.Tensor):
        return torch.full_like(like, float(out))
    if out.shape != like.shape:
        out = out.expand_as(like) if out.dim() <= like.dim() else out
    return out

        KeyError: If ``key`` is not in :data:`CATALOG`.
    """
    if key not in CATALOG:
        raise KeyError(f"Unknown catalogue entry {key!r}. Available: {', '.join(CATALOG)}")
    spec = copy.deepcopy(CATALOG[key])
    spec.update(overrides)
    return CustomPDE.from_dict(spec)

def get_pde_spec(name: str) -> PDESpec:
    """Resolve a config key or display name (case-insensitive) to its spec.

    Raises:
        KeyError: If ``name`` matches no registered PDE.
    """
    spec = _LOOKUP.get(name.strip().lower())
    if spec is None:
        available = ", ".join(s.key for s in PDE_SPECS)
        raise KeyError(f"Unknown PDE {name!r}. Available: {available}")
    return spec

Base class for PDEs solved by PINNs.

A subclass provides the physics:

  • :meth:compute_residual — the PDE operator applied to the network.
  • :meth:_create_initial_condition — u(x, t0) for its IC types.
  • :meth:_exact_solution — a closed-form solution, when one exists.
  • time_order = 2 for second-order-in-time PDEs; the initial loss then also enforces u_t(x, t0) = initial_condition["velocity"] (default 0).

The base class owns everything else: derivatives, collocation sampling, boundary conditions and the composite loss. boundary_conditions in the config maps a kind to its options; every spatial axis gets the condition on both faces:

  • dirichlet: {"value": v} or {"left": a, "right": b} (the lower / upper face), or {"type": "exact"} to take values from the exact solution;
  • neumann: {"value": g} — du/dx_axis = g on both faces;
  • periodic: {} — u and du/dx_axis agree on opposite faces.

exact_solution: {} in the config means the problem has no closed-form solution; :meth:exact_solution then returns None.

def __init__(self, config: PDEConfig, bandit_sampler=None):
    """Initialize PDE with given configuration.

    Args:
        config: Configuration dataclass.
        bandit_sampler: Optional :class:`ResidualBanditSampler` for the
            ``adaptive`` strategy; built lazily with defaults when omitted.
    """
    self.config = config
    domain: Any = config.domain
    self.domain: list[tuple[float, float]]
    self.bandit_sampler = bandit_sampler

    # One (lo, hi) pair per spatial axis; a bare (lo, hi) means one axis.
    if not domain:
        self.domain = [(0.0, 1.0)]
    elif isinstance(domain[0], (list, tuple)):
        self.domain = [(float(lo), float(hi)) for lo, hi in domain]
    else:
        self.domain = [(float(domain[0]), float(domain[1]))]

    # Update config with normalized domain format
    self.config.domain = self.domain

    # Handle time_domain/t_domain property
    time_domain: Any
    if hasattr(config, "time_domain"):
        time_domain = config.time_domain
    elif hasattr(config, "t_domain"):
        time_domain = config.t_domain
    else:
        time_domain = [0.0, 1.0]
    # Time-marching (H04): when set, collocation points and data records are taken on
    # [t0, time_cutoff] only; ``PDETrainer.train_windows`` moves it window by window.
    self.time_cutoff: float | None = None

    # Convert time_domain to tuple if it's a list
    if isinstance(time_domain, list):
        time_domain = tuple(time_domain)
    # ``None`` here is replaced by the observations' time range further down.
    self.time_domain: tuple[float, float] = time_domain

    # Setup device - Handle device explicitly and carefully
    if hasattr(config, "device") and config.device is not None:
        # If config.device is already a torch.device object, use it directly
        if isinstance(config.device, torch.device):
            self.device = config.device
        else:
            # Try to convert string to torch.device
            try:
                self.device = torch.device(str(config.device))
            except Exception:
                print(f"Warning: Invalid device '{config.device}', falling back to CPU")
                self.device = torch.device("cpu")
    else:
        # Fallback to CPU if no device specified
        self.device = torch.device("cpu")

    # Ensure config has the same device
    self.config.device = self.device

    # Store dimensionality
    self.dimension = config.dimension

    # Make sure parameters exist but preserve any existing parameters
    if not hasattr(config, "parameters"):
        config.parameters = {}
    elif config.parameters is None:
        config.parameters = {}

    # Register trainable parameters as nn.Parameter (inverse-problem mode).
    # In forward mode this dict stays empty and adds no behaviour.
    self._trainable_params: nn.ParameterDict = nn.ParameterDict()
    trainable_names = list(getattr(config, "trainable_parameters", []) or [])
    initial_guesses = dict(getattr(config, "parameter_initial_guesses", {}) or {})
    # Snapshot the original (true) values BEFORE the parameters become
    # trainable, so we can plot a reference line in the dashboard.
    self._true_parameters: dict[str, float] = {}
    for name in trainable_names:
        true_val = _as_scalar(name, config.parameters.get(name))
        if true_val is not None:
            self._true_parameters[name] = true_val
        init_val = _as_scalar(
            name, initial_guesses.get(name, true_val if true_val is not None else 1.0)
        )
        self._trainable_params[name] = nn.Parameter(torch.tensor(init_val, device=self.device))

    # Load observation data (used by the data-fitting loss in inverse mode).
    self.observation_data: dict[str, torch.Tensor] | None = self._load_observation_data(
        getattr(config, "observation_data", None)
    )
    # No time window of its own (a Well dataset, whose trajectory length can
    # differ by file): span the time range of the observations, else [0, 1].
    if self.time_domain is None:
        if self.observation_data is not None:
            t = self.observation_data["t"]
            self.time_domain = (float(t.min()), float(t.max()))
        else:
            self.time_domain = (0.0, 1.0)
        self.config.time_domain = self.time_domain

    self.initial_condition = self._create_initial_condition(
        dict(config.initial_condition or {})
    )
    self.boundary_conditions = self._parse_boundary_conditions(config.boundary_conditions or {})
    self._fixed_points: dict[tuple[str, int], Any] = {}

    # Setup neural network parameters if not specified
    if self.config.input_dim is None:
        self.config.input_dim = self.dimension + 1  # Spatial dimensions + time

    if self.config.output_dim is None:
        self.config.output_dim = 1  # Default to single output (u)

def get_parameter(self, name: str, default=None, required: bool = False):
    """Safely get a parameter value with validation.

    When ``name`` has been registered as a trainable parameter (inverse
    problem mode), the live ``nn.Parameter`` tensor is returned so that
    downstream residual computations build the autograd graph through it.
    Otherwise the plain float from ``config.parameters`` is returned.

    Args:
        name: Parameter name
        default: Default value if parameter not found
        required: Whether parameter is required (raises error if missing)

    Returns:
        Parameter value (``nn.Parameter`` if trainable, else float)

    Raises:
        ValueError: If required parameter is missing
    """
    # Trainable param takes precedence over the static config value.
    trainable = getattr(self, "_trainable_params", None)
    if trainable is not None and name in trainable:
        return trainable[name]

    if not hasattr(self.config, "parameters") or self.config.parameters is None:
        if required:
            raise ValueError(f"Required parameter '{name}' not found in config")
        return default

    value = self.config.parameters.get(name, default)
    if value is None and required:
        raise ValueError(f"Required parameter '{name}' not found in config")
    return value

def generate_synthetic_observations(
    self,
    n_points: int = 200,
    noise_std: float = 0.0,
    seed: int | None = 0,
) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
    """Sample noisy observations from the analytical solution.

    Useful for inverse-problem demos and CI tests: pick uniform points in
    the domain, evaluate ``self.exact_solution``, optionally add Gaussian
    noise, and store the result on ``self.observation_data`` so the next
    ``compute_loss`` call automatically picks it up.

    Args:
        n_points: Number of observations.
        noise_std: Standard deviation of the additive Gaussian noise.
        seed: Seed for the points and the noise; ``None`` leaves it unseeded.

    Returns:
        ``{"x", "t", "u"}`` tensors, also stored on ``self.observation_data``.

    Raises:
        ValueError: If the PDE has no exact solution configured.
    """
    gen = torch.Generator(device="cpu")
    if seed is not None:
        gen.manual_seed(int(seed))

    spatial_dims = max(int(self.dimension), 1)
    x_cols = []
    for d in range(spatial_dims):
        lo, hi = self.domain[d]
        x_cols.append(torch.rand(n_points, 1, generator=gen) * (hi - lo) + lo)
    x = (
        torch.cat(x_cols, dim=1).to(self.device)
        if spatial_dims > 1
        else x_cols[0].to(self.device)
    )

    t_lo, t_hi = self.time_domain[0], self.time_domain[1]
    t = (torch.rand(n_points, 1, generator=gen) * (t_hi - t_lo) + t_lo).to(self.device)

    # Temporarily unregister the trainable params so ``get_parameter``
    # returns the TRUE values from ``config.parameters`` (the ones
    # snapshotted in ``_true_parameters``) rather than the current guess.
    # Without this, synthetic obs generated in inverse mode would already
    # encode the wrong α and the trainer would converge to the guess
    # rather than recovering the true value.
    saved_params = self._trainable_params if hasattr(self, "_trainable_params") else None
    try:
        if saved_params is not None and self._true_parameters:
            self._trainable_params = nn.ParameterDict()
        if not self.has_exact_solution:
            raise ValueError(
                f"{self.config.name}: synthetic observations need a configured exact_solution"
            )
        with torch.no_grad():
            u = self.exact_solution(x, t)
            assert u is not None  # has_exact_solution was checked above
            if noise_std and noise_std > 0:
                noise = torch.randn(u.shape, generator=gen).to(self.device) * float(noise_std)
                u = u + noise
    finally:
        if saved_params is not None:
            self._trainable_params = saved_params

    self.observation_data = {"x": x, "t": t, "u": u}
    return self.observation_data

Sum of the pure second derivatives of f along each column of x.

x must be the leaf tensor f was computed from (requires_grad). Differentiating with respect to the whole tensor and then taking a column is what makes this correct in more than one dimension; a column slice x[:, d:d+1] is not part of the graph.

Source code in pinnrl/pdes/pde_base.py 
def laplacian(self, f: torch.Tensor, x: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor:
    """Sum of the pure second derivatives of ``f`` along each column of ``x``.

    ``x`` must be the leaf tensor ``f`` was computed from (``requires_grad``).
    Differentiating with respect to the whole tensor and then taking a column
    is what makes this correct in more than one dimension; a column slice
    ``x[:, d:d+1]`` is not part of the graph.
    """
    grad = self._grad(f, x)
    lap = torch.zeros_like(f)
    for d in range(x.shape[1]):
        lap = lap + self._grad(grad[:, d : d + 1], x)[:, d : d + 1]
    return lap

def compute_derivatives(
    self,
    model: torch.nn.Module,
    x: torch.Tensor,
    t: torch.Tensor,
    temporal_derivatives: Iterable[int] | None = None,
    spatial_derivatives: Iterable[int] | None = None,
) -> dict[str, torch.Tensor]:
    """Evaluate ``u = model([x, t])`` and the requested derivatives.

    Args:
        model: Neural network model.
        x: Spatial coordinates, shape ``(N, dimension)``.
        t: Time coordinates, shape ``(N, 1)``.
        temporal_derivatives: Orders of ``∂/∂t`` to return (1 and/or 2).
        spatial_derivatives: Orders of the pure ``∂/∂x_d`` derivatives to
            return (1 to 4).

    Returns a dict with ``"u"`` and, for the requested orders only:

    * time: ``"dt"``, ``"dt2"``;
    * space, 1-D: ``"dx"``, ``"dx2"``, ``"dx3"``, ``"dx4"``;
    * space, n-D: pure derivatives per axis, ``"dx1"``, ``"dx1x1"``, ... ``"dx2x2"``;
    * ``"laplacian"`` whenever order 2 is requested.

    Raises:
        ValueError: For temporal orders above 2 or spatial orders above 4.
    """
    temporal = sorted(set(temporal_derivatives or ()) - {0})
    spatial = sorted(set(spatial_derivatives or ()) - {0})
    if temporal and temporal[-1] > 2:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Temporal derivative order {temporal[-1]} is not supported. Maximum order is 2."
        )
    if spatial and spatial[-1] > 4:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Spatial derivative order {spatial[-1]} is not supported. Maximum order is 4."
        )

    x, t, u = self._prepare_inputs(model, x, t)
    derivatives = {"u": u}

    current = u
    for order in range(1, (temporal[-1] if temporal else 0) + 1):
        current = self._grad(current, t)
        if order in temporal:
            derivatives["dt" if order == 1 else f"dt{order}"] = current

    for dim in range(self.dimension):
        current = u
        for order in range(1, (spatial[-1] if spatial else 0) + 1):
            current = self._grad(current, x)[:, dim : dim + 1]
            if order not in spatial:
                continue
            if self.dimension == 1:
                key = "dx" if order == 1 else f"dx{order}"
            else:
                key = "d" + f"x{dim + 1}" * order
            derivatives[key] = current

    if 2 in spatial:
        if self.dimension == 1:
            derivatives["laplacian"] = derivatives["dx2"]
        else:
            derivatives["laplacian"] = sum(
                derivatives["d" + f"x{d + 1}" * 2] for d in range(self.dimension)
            )
    return derivatives

def exact_solution(self, x: torch.Tensor, t: torch.Tensor) -> torch.Tensor | None:
    """Closed-form ``u(x, t)``, or ``None`` when ``exact_solution`` is not configured."""
    if not self.has_exact_solution:

    # Exact solutions start from the IC at t = 0; shift so they hold for any t0.
    return self._exact_solution(x, t - float(self.time_domain[0]))

def sampling_time_domain(self) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """The time span points are drawn from: the time domain, cut at ``time_cutoff`` when set."""
